item.title: Empirical tuberculosis treatment in infants living with HIV hospitalised with severe pneumonia in Africa (EMPIRICAL): a multicentre, randomised, open-label, 2 × 2 factorial, controlled superiority trial.
item.dc:creator: Domínguez-Rodríguez S, Tagarro A, Moraleda C, Buck WC, Mujuru H, Chabala C, Mvalo T, Iroh-Tam PY, Cossa A, Madrid L, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Domínguez-Rodríguez S, Tagarro A, Moraleda C, Buck WC, Mujuru H, Chabala C, Mvalo T, Iroh-Tam PY, Cossa A, Madrid L, et al.
Journal: Lancet (London, England) | DOI: 10.1016/S0140-6736(26)01418-2
Published: 2026-Nov-14
PMID: 43020097



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mortality among infants with severe HIV-associated pneumonia remains high globally. The EMPIRICAL trial evaluated whether empirical tuberculosis treatment (eTB-T) improves survival compared with the currently recommended microbiologically and clinically guided strategy. METHODS: This multicentre, open-label, group-sequential designed, 2×2 factorial, randomised, controlled, superiority trial was conducted in 19 hospitals across Côte d'Ivoire, Malawi, Mozambique, Uganda, Zambia, and Zimbabwe. Infants aged 28-365 days admitted with severe HIV-associated pneumonia, without a current tuberculosis diagnosis or contact, were centrally and individually randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) using a secure web-based system stratified by site and severity. A computer-generated block randomisation schedule was used, with fixed blocks of eight allocations (two allocations to each factorial treatment group) within each stratum. Participants received standard of care (SoC) comprising treatment for bacterial (WHO-recommended antibiotics) and Pneumocystis jirovecii (cotrimoxazole and steroids) pneumonia, SoC plus 15 days of oral valganciclovir (16 mg/kg per 12 h), or SoC plus 6 months of tuberculosis treatment (isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol for 2 months, plus isoniazid and rifampicin for 4 subsequent months), or both interventions combined. Here, we report the comparison between the eTB-T (ie, SoC plus tuberculosis treatment and SoC plus oral valganciclovir plus tuberculosis treatment) and non-eTB-T (ie, SoC or SoC plus 15 days of oral valganciclovir) groups. Nasopharyngeal aspirates, stools for Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra testing, and urine for tuberculosis lipoarabinomannan assay were collected at recruitment. In the non-eTB-T groups, tuberculosis treatment was initiated if microbiological results collected at recruitment yielded positive results or if, during follow-up, the treating clinician suspected tuberculosis on clinical grounds, including radiological findings, in accordance with routine clinical practice and guidelines. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality (at 15 days and 360 days). Survival was estimated using flexible parametric models with covariate-adjusted conditional estimates; missing data were imputed by chained equations. The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03915366) and is now complete. FINDINGS: Between March 15, 2020, and Jan 31, 2024, 563 participants were enrolled; 558 were analysed after excluding five patients who did not meet eligibility criteria. 276 participants were allocated to the eTB-T groups (n=140 eTB-T and n=136 valganciclovir plus eTB-T) and 282 to the non-eTB-T groups (n=142 SoC and n=140 valganciclovir). 17 (6%) of 276 in the eTB-T groups and 20 (7%) of 282 in the non-eTB-T groups were lost to follow-up. Median age was 4·4 months (IQR 3·2-7·4) and 274 (49%) of participants were female and 284 (51%) were male. In the non-eTB-T groups, 130 (46%) of 282 participants eventually initiated tuberculosis treatment at a median of 4·0 days (IQR 3·0-15·0) after recruitment due to positive microbiological findings in 55 (20%) cases (53 confirmed by tuberculosis lipoarabinomannan assay and two by nasopharyngeal aspirates Xpert MTB/RIF) or clinical decision in 75 (27%) cases. There was no evidence of interaction between valganciclovir and eTB-T (adjusted hazard ratio 1·19, 95% CI 0·73-1·95; pheterogeneity=0·4836). At 12 months, 132 (48%) of 276 participants in eTB-T groups and 121 (43%) of 282 participants in non-eTB-T groups died. In the eTB-T groups, the adjusted hazard ratio for death was 1·12 (95% CI 0·87-1·43; p=0·3868). At 15 days, the odds ratio was 1·24 (95% CI 0·83-1·84; p=0·2950). Serious adverse events did not differ between groups (1·19, 0·82-1·73; p=0·3523). There were no treatment-related deaths. The most common adverse events were elevation of transaminases (72 [26%] cases in the eTB-T groups and 74 [26%] in the non-eTB-T group), anaemia (163 [59%] cases in the eTB-T groups and 169 [60%] in the non-eTB-T groups), and infectious disease requiring antimicrobial treatment (161 [58%] cases in the eTB-T groups and 176 [62%] in the non-eTB-T groups). INTERPRETATION: In contrast to empirical treatment with valganciclovir, there was no evidence that eTB-T was superior to a clinically and microbiologically guided strategy in reducing all-cause mortality among infants with HIV-associated pneumonia. However, the high proportion of infants who eventually initiated tuberculosis treatment during follow-up in the non-eTB-T groups might have reduced the contrast between strategies and attenuated the ability to detect differences in outcomes. item.title: A single-cell lung cancer atlas reveals cellular and molecular drivers of metastasis and clinical outcome.
item.dc:creator: Jurmeister P, Keyl P, Mochmann LH, Bergmayr L, Schleich K, Chimal Calderon E, Engelhardt-Schott F, Klingler D, Papić D, Wolff J, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Jurmeister P, Keyl P, Mochmann LH, Bergmayr L, Schleich K, Chimal Calderon E, Engelhardt-Schott F, Klingler D, Papić D, Wolff J, et al.
Journal: Nature cancer | DOI: 10.1038/s43018-026-01260-w
Published: 2026-Nov-12
PMID: 43020953



Abstract:
Non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, characterized by extensive cellular and molecular heterogeneity. Here, to capture this complexity, we present LuCaS+, a multicenter single-cell RNA sequencing atlas comprising over 2.5 million nuclei from 454 clinically annotated patients with NSCLC with long-term follow-up. LuCaS+ consists of a discovery dataset (Berlin and Cologne, 364 patients) and an independent validation dataset (Munich, 90 patients). Leveraging this dataset, we identified tumor subpopulations with high metastatic potential associated with oncogenic signaling, immune evasion and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. In early-stage adenocarcinoma (lung adenocarcinoma), these cells showed strong prognostic value. Integrating tumor and microenvironmental cell profiles improved survival prediction across all stages, identifying distinct tumor-immune-stromal interaction patterns. These included monocyte- and fibroblast-driven inflammation (lung adenocarcinoma), VEGF-TGFβ-mediated angiogenic feedback loops (lung squamous cell carcinoma) and immune-permissive niches promoting antitumor immunity. LuCaS+ offers a clinically anchored single-cell resource to enable personalized, biology-driven therapies in NSCLC.

item.title: Cognitive and physiological responses to prolonged video viewing: Activities of the autonomic nervous system and hypothalamo-pituitary-adrenal axis in relation to video interest.
item.dc:creator: Matsui H, Tanabe R, Mogi R, Sugiura Y, Yokomachi H, Yokoyama T
item.description:
Authors: Matsui H, Tanabe R, Mogi R, Sugiura Y, Yokomachi H, Yokoyama T
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0362672
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43019370



Abstract:
In recent years, online lectures and conferences have become widespread, but prolonged video viewing has been suggested to affect psychological state and physiological regulation. However, few studies have objectively examined how such viewing influences autonomic and endocrine activity. This study aimed to evaluate changes in autonomic nervous system (ANS) activity and hypothalamo-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis activity during the viewing of high- and low-interest videos. Twenty-six university students (10 males, 16 females; aged 21-24 years) watched high-interest (comedy) and low-interest (lecture) videos (90 minutes each). After viewing each video, they recorded subjective ratings of concentration, comprehension, interest, and fatigue. To assess autonomic nervous system activity, heart rate (HR) and heart rate variability (HRV) analyses, including the low-frequency (LF)/high-frequency (HF) ratio (LF/HF), LF and HF power, and very low-frequency (VLF) power, were performed. As stress markers, saliva samples were collected before, during, and after video viewing to measure cortisol, amylase, and chromogranin A (CgA). Subjective ratings showed that scores for concentration, comprehension, and interest were significantly higher, and fatigue was lower during the high-interest video. Regarding physiological indicators, significant main effects of time were observed for heart rate, LF/HF, LF, HF, and VLF, with overall patterns of lower heart rate and LF/HF and higher LF, HF, and VLF power during viewing. Salivary cortisol also decreased over time during both videos, demonstrating a significant main effect of time. However, no significant changes were observed in salivary amylase or chromogranin A. Furthermore, a significant interest × time interaction was observed for HR, but not for the other physiological indicators. A significant main effect of interest was observed only for LF. These findings indicate that the video conditions differed in subjective cognitive evaluation, with condition-dependent temporal changes detected for HR, whereas no significant interest × time interactions were detected for the other physiological indicators.

item.title: A primary study of inverted right-angle configuration cannulated screws fixation of femoral neck fracture based on elaborated 3-dimensional features of the femoral head and neck region.
item.dc:creator: Liu C, Zhang H, Liu Y, Liu P, Hou Y
item.description:
Authors: Liu C, Zhang H, Liu Y, Liu P, Hou Y
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361871
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43019351



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: CT-based three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction was used to analyze the detailed anatomical morphology of the femoral head-neck region, and a modified inverted right-angle cannulated screw configuration was proposed to reduce the risk of posterosuperior screw in-out-in (IOI) placement during femoral neck fracture fixation. METHODS: Imaging data from 22 patients (12 males and 10 females; mean age, 52.5 ± 16.8 years) were retrospectively analyzed. CT data of both hips were imported into Mimics to construct 3D digital femoral models for morphologic analysis and screw trajectory simulation. Based on the observed anterior offset of the femoral head-neck canal and the sloped posterosuperior cortex of the femoral neck, a modified inverted right-angle screw configuration and a negative anteversion fluoroscopic view were proposed. Technical feasibility was preliminarily illustrated in two patients with femoral neck fractures. RESULTS: The femoral head-neck axis showed an anterior offset relative to the proximal femoral axis, which may increase the risk of posterosuperior IOI screw trajectory with the traditional inverted triangle configuration. In the 3D simulation, the modified inverted right-angle configuration placed the posterosuperior screw within the proposed safety zone. The negative anteversion fluoroscopic view appeared useful for identifying potential IOI screw trajectory. Technical feasibility of the proposed configuration was illustrated in two patients with femoral neck fractures, in whom no postoperative IOI screw displacement was observed on CT. CONCLUSION: The anatomical features of the femoral head-neck region may contribute to the risk of posterosuperior IOI screw trajectory with the traditional inverted triangle configuration. In this CT-based morphologic and simulation study, the modified inverted right-angle configuration showed a more favorable simulated position of the posterosuperior screw within the proposed safety zone, while negative anteversion fluoroscopy may help identify potential IOI screw trajectory. These preliminary findings require further validation through biomechanical studies and larger comparative clinical investigations.

item.title: Dose-dependent hepatorenal toxicity of polystyrene microplastics in BALB/c mice.
item.dc:creator: Iftikhar S, Alnashiri HM, Akhtar M, Ahsan Z, Latif M, El-Shabasy A, Soliman MM
item.description:
Authors: Iftikhar S, Alnashiri HM, Akhtar M, Ahsan Z, Latif M, El-Shabasy A, Soliman MM
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0362569
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43019317



Abstract:
Microplastics have emerged as pervasive environmental contaminants with increasing concern regarding their potential adverse effects on mammalian health. However, comprehensive evaluations of the dose-related hepatorenal toxicity of polystyrene microplastics (PS-MPs) remain limited. This study investigated the effects of oral exposure to PS-MPs on hepatic and renal function in BALB/c mice. Animals were randomly assigned to four groups (n = 10/group) and orally administered 0 (control), 10, 20, or 30 mg PS-MPs/kg body weight/day for 28 consecutive days. Hepatorenal toxicity was evaluated using serum biochemical biomarkers, histopathological examination, semi-quantitative lesion scoring, and Pearson's correlation analysis. PS-MP exposure produced dose-related increases in serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT; P = 0.0247), aspartate aminotransferase (AST; P = 0.0192), alkaline phosphatase (ALP; P = 0.0044), bilirubin (P = 0.0045), creatinine (P = 0.0029), and urea (P = 0.0006), with generally higher values observed at increasing PS-MPs doses indicating hepatic and renal dysfunction. Histopathological assessment demonstrated increasing severity of hepatic inflammatory infiltration, hepatocellular degeneration, necrosis, sinusoidal dilatation, and renal tubular epithelial degeneration/necrosis with increasing PS-MP dose. Semi-quantitative histopathological scores differed significantly among groups (Kruskal-Wallis, P < 0.0001), with the greatest lesion severity observed in the high-dose group. Pearson's correlation analysis revealed significant positive correlations between creatinine and urea (r = 0.7628, P < 0.0001) and between ALP and bilirubin (r = 0.5229, P = 0.0087), supporting the biochemical evidence of renal and hepatobiliary dysfunction. In conclusion, oral exposure to PS-MPs was associated with hepatorenal toxicity,characterized by biochemical alterations and increasing histopathological injury with increasing exposure dose. These findings provide experimental evidence of the adverse effects of PS-MPs on mammalian liver and kidney function and contribute to a better understanding of the potential health risks associated with chronic microplastic exposure.

item.title: Early vs Routine Oral Nutritional Supplementation During Concurrent Chemoradiotherapy for Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
item.dc:creator: Su L, Bai ZG, Liu RQ, Qin WJ, Chen ZL, Li AC, Ma K, Su JJ, Zhang SF, Lu HJ, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Su L, Bai ZG, Liu RQ, Qin WJ, Chen ZL, Li AC, Ma K, Su JJ, Zhang SF, Lu HJ, et al.
Journal: JAMA oncology | DOI: 10.1001/jamaoncol.2026.4535
Published: 2026-Nov-12
PMID: 43018988



Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Oral nutritional supplementation (ONS), providing supplementary oral nutrition in addition to usual food, is widely used during concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) for nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), but its optimal timing and cost utility remain uncertain. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate efficacy and explore cost utility of early ONS in patients with NPC undergoing CCRT. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter, open-label, randomized clinical trial was conducted at 6 Chinese tertiary hospitals from July 2021 to May 2025. Eligible patients were aged 18 to 70 years with newly diagnosed stage II to IVA NPC, a Patient-Generated Subjective Global Assessment (PG-SGA) score of 0 to 8, and planned CCRT. Key exclusions included oral intake less than 60% of requirements for 3 days or longer, inability or unwillingness to receive concurrent chemotherapy, and inability to receive oral or enteral nutrition. Data were analyzed from November 2025 to March 2026. INTERVENTION: Participants were randomized 1:1 to early ONS at CCRT start or routine ONS after prespecified nutritional decline. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point was the incidence of more than 5% weight loss from baseline to CCRT completion. Secondary end points included PG-SGA score, the incidence of grade 3 or higher radiation-induced oral mucositis (RIOM), quality of life (European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire Core 30), and radiotherapy interruption. Cost utility measures included total cost, utility, and incremental cost utility ratio. RESULTS: Of 242 patients screened, 236 patients were randomized, and the prespecified modified intention-to-treat population included 216 patients (mean [SD] age, 46.62 [11.19] years; 168 [77.8%] male), with 107 receiving early ONS and 109 receiving routine ONS. More than 5% weight loss occurred in 70 participants (65.4% ) in the early ONS group, compared with 88 participants (80.7%) in the routine ONS group (relative risk [RR], 0.81; 95% CI, 0.68-0.96; P = .01). An intention-to-treat analysis including all randomized participants yielded a similar estimate (RR, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.65-0.93). In the modified intention-to-treat population, grade 3 or higher RIOM occurred in 15 participants (14.0%) in the early ONS group vs 29 participants (26.6%) in the routine ONS group (RR, 0.53; 95% CI, 0.30-0.93). Best-case costs were $9560.56 in the early ONS group vs $9685.23 in the routine ONS group, with quality-adjusted life-years of 0.1144 vs 0.1132, respectively. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This randomized clinical trial found that early ONS reduced clinically meaningful weight loss during CCRT; exploratory analyses suggested potential benefits for severe RIOM and a potentially favorable short-term economic profile. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04823468.

item.title: Artificial Intelligence Models to Predict Recurrence in Patients with Differentiated Thyroid Cancer: A PROBAST + AI Systematic Review of Clinical Applicability.
item.dc:creator: Solis-Pazmino P, Samaniego AF, Golbert L, Laurini de Souza Meyer E, Pilatuna EA, Suñé Mattevi V, Moposita Molina F, Nienow D, Guidolin K, Berton Eidt L, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Solis-Pazmino P, Samaniego AF, Golbert L, Laurini de Souza Meyer E, Pilatuna EA, Suñé Mattevi V, Moposita Molina F, Nienow D, Guidolin K, Berton Eidt L, et al.
Journal: Thyroid : official journal of the American Thyroid Association | DOI: 10.1177/10507256261504546
Published: 2026-Nov-12
PMID: 43018984



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC) generally carries an excellent prognosis, yet recurrence occurs in up to 8-9% of patients. Artificial intelligence (AI) models are increasingly proposed to predict DTC recurrence; however, their methodological quality and clinical readiness are poorly defined. We conducted a systematic review to evaluate the methodological quality, risk of bias, and applicability of these models using the PROBAST + AI framework. METHODS: We searched Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane databases, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception to July 13, 2026. Eligible studies included original research developing or validating AI models for recurrence in DTC. Model quality (for development), risk of bias (for evaluation), and applicability were assessed using the PROBAST + AI framework, with a focus on discrimination, calibration, and validation strategies (PROSPERO; registration number [CRD420251004644]). RESULTS: Of 673 records screened, 34 studies were included (21 unique datasets and 13 UCI-derived publications), encompassing 21,267 patients with a recurrence rate of 7.8%. Most were developed in Asian cohorts (17 of 21 datasets) and were structured clinical/tabular variables (82.4%), including demographic, clinical, laboratory, and pathological data, whereas the remaining models incorporated multimodal inputs such as imaging-derived or radiomic features. Notably, nearly one quarter of included studies (13 of 34, 38%) represented reanalysis of a single dataset. Discrimination was reported in 22 of 34 studies (64.7%) (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC] 0.67-1.00), though only 10 studies assessed calibration, none with standardized metrics. The PROBAST + AI assessment revealed high overall quality concerns in 26 of 34 (76.5%) development studies due to reliance on single-center cohorts, inadequate handling of missing data, and absence of external validation. Only 6 of 34 included studies (17.6%) were judged to have low overall quality concern, whereas 17 of 34 (50.0%) were rated as having low applicability concern. CONCLUSIONS: AI models for predicting DTC recurrence show promising discriminatory performance but have substantial methodological shortcomings in development, and a lack of calibration and external validation necessary for clinical use. Given the guidelines' emphasis on risk-adapted de-escalation of therapy, the development of robust, validated, and clinically calibrated AI tools is a priority. Current evidence remains insufficient to support routine clinical use.

item.title: Perioperative Camrelizumab Plus Chemotherapy in Locally Advanced Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
item.dc:creator: Liu F, Zhang Y, Ma H, Zhang W, Chen B, Sun J, Ding J, Yuan H, Wang Y, Cao W, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Liu F, Zhang Y, Ma H, Zhang W, Chen B, Sun J, Ding J, Yuan H, Wang Y, Cao W, et al.
Journal: JAMA oncology | DOI: 10.1001/jamaoncol.2026.4642
Published: 2026-Nov-12
PMID: 43018983



Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Despite multimodal treatment, recurrence remains common in patients with resectable locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). Whether perioperative chemoimmunotherapy improves long-term outcomes remains uncertain. OBJECTIVE: To estimate the effect of perioperative camrelizumab plus chemotherapy on event-free survival (EFS) compared with standard surgery-based treatment in patients with resectable locally advanced HNSCC. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: The CAMORAL trial was a multicenter, phase 2 randomized clinical trial conducted at 4 academic hospitals in China between October 2020 and March 2024, with data cutoff on April 11, 2025. Patients aged 18 to 75 years with untreated, resectable stage III to IVB HNSCC were assigned to neoadjuvant-adjuvant treatment or control. Analyses used the intention-to-treat population. Data were analyzed from May 2025 to February 2026. INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomized (1:1) to receive two 21-day cycles of neoadjuvant camrelizumab, 200 mg, plus albumin-bound paclitaxel and carboplatin followed by surgery, risk-adapted adjuvant therapy, and maintenance camrelizumab for up to 15 cycles; or upfront surgery followed by standard risk-adapted adjuvant therapy. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point was 2-year EFS. Secondary end points included major pathological response (MPR), pathological complete response (pCR), overall survival, 2-year distant metastasis-free survival, 2-year locoregional recurrence-free survival, and safety. RESULTS: Of 125 included patients, 99 (79.2%) were male, and the mean (SD) age was 56.3 (11.7) years. A total of 63 patients were assigned to the neoadjuvant-adjuvant group and 62 to the control group; the median (IQR) follow-up was 24.6 (16.8-36.5) months. A total of 103 (82.4%) had oral cavity primary tumors. Among 125 patients, the 2-year EFS rate was 77.8% (95% CI, 63.6-87.0) in the neoadjuvant-adjuvant group compared with 46.1% (95% CI, 31.3-59.6) in the control group (hazard ratio, 0.34; 95% CI, 0.17-0.68; P = .001). MPR and pCR were 47.6% (95% CI, 34.9-60.6) and 25.4% (95% CI, 15.3-37.9), respectively, in the neoadjuvant-adjuvant group, with no MPR or pCR events in the control group. The 2-year overall survival rates were 92.0% and 69.1%, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.25; 95% CI, 0.10-0.64); the hazard ratio of 2-year distant metastasis-free survival was 0.15 (95% CI, 0.03-0.68). Grade 3 or higher treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 50 of 63 patients (79.4%) in the neoadjuvant-adjuvant group and 35 of 62 patients (56.5%) in the control group; 1 fatal treatment-emergent adverse event occurred in the control group. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this phase 2 randomized clinical trial, perioperative camrelizumab plus chemotherapy significantly improved EFS with manageable toxic effects, supporting evaluation of intensified perioperative immune priming in resectable HNSCC. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ChiCTR.org.cn Identifier: ChiCTR2000037980.

item.title: A Preoperative Grading System for Endoscopic Sinus Surgery.
item.dc:creator: Williams E, Minesinger K, Guevara G, Casiano RR, Palacio A, Levine CG
item.description:
Authors: Williams E, Minesinger K, Guevara G, Casiano RR, Palacio A, Levine CG
Journal: JAMA otolaryngology-- head & neck surgery | DOI: 10.1001/jamaoto.2026.3451
Published: 2026-Nov-12
PMID: 43018980



Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) is common, yet one-third of patients do not achieve clinically meaningful improvement after endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS). Existing preoperative measures capture only a portion of the prognostic landscape, and no tool integrates patient-reported phenotype, symptom severity, and objective imaging into a single ordinal index for surgical prognosis. OBJECTIVE: To develop a CRS Severity Index (CRS-SI) that integrates patient-reported symptom phenotypes, characterized across symptom duration categories, with objective imaging measures to estimate the probability of clinically meaningful improvement after ESS. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Prospective cohort study with longitudinal data collected from academic tertiary care rhinology clinics between January 2020 and May 2025; follow-up was assessed at 3, 6, and 12 months after surgery. Participants were consecutive patients with CRS aged 16 to 95 years for whom medical management failed and who underwent ESS. EXPOSURES: Baseline 22-item Sino-Nasal Outcome Test (SNOT-22) measures, symptom phenotype dimensions derived from multiple correspondence analysis, polyp status, Lund-Mackay, and Lund-Kennedy scores. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was clinically meaningful improvement, defined as SNOT-22 improvement of at least 8.9 points from baseline to follow-up. Seven candidate predictors were organized into clinical (baseline SNOT-22, latent symptom phenotype dimensions, polyp status) and imaging (Lund-Mackay, Lund-Kennedy, frontal opacification) arms. CRS-SI was derived using sequential sequestration and conjunctive consolidation. RESULTS: Of 488 eligible patients with at least 1 postoperative SNOT-22, 450 with complete clinical and imaging grading data comprised the analytic cohort. Among 450 patients (mean [SD] age, 55.5 [16.3] years; 54.7% [246 of 450] male), 64% achieved clinically meaningful improvement. Of 7 candidate predictors, 6 met bivariate screening criteria (rank-biserial |r|≥0.1 with 95% CI excluding 0). Sequential sequestration selected baseline SNOT-22 severity and a headache and/or chemosensory-dominant symptom phenotype as clinical classifiers, and Lund-Mackay and Lund-Kennedy scores as imaging classifiers. The 4-grade CRS-SI produced a monotonic improvement gradient (grade 1, 81% [95% CI, 72%-88%] to grade 4, 29% [95% CI, 19%-40%]), with a risk difference of 52.5 (95% CI, 39.3-65.7) percentage points between best and worst grades. Discrimination was moderate (C statistic, 0.692; 95% CI, 0.643-0.740) and exceeded imaging grading alone; bootstrap calibration slope, 1.00 (95% CI, 0.77-1.31). Performance was consistent across CRS phenotypes and time points. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, a 4-level CRS Severity Index integrating patient-reported symptom profiles with computed tomography and endoscopic imaging stratified improvement after ESS across a 52 percentage-point gradient. If validated externally, the CRS-SI may support preoperative counseling and clinical trial stratification.

item.title: Izalontamab Brengitecan in Recurrent or Metastatic Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: The PANKU-Esophagus01 Randomized Clinical Trial.
item.dc:creator: Lu Z, Huang Z, Meng X, Fan Y, Wu T, Pang Q, Wang F, Zhang Y, Gao S, Liu T, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Lu Z, Huang Z, Meng X, Fan Y, Wu T, Pang Q, Wang F, Zhang Y, Gao S, Liu T, et al.
Journal: JAMA | DOI: 10.1001/jama.2026.20250
Published: 2026-Nov-12
PMID: 43018949



Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Effective therapy remains lacking for patients with advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) whose disease progressed after standard treatment. Izalontamab brengitecan, an epidermal growth factor receptor and human epidermal growth factor receptor 3 bispecific antibody-drug conjugate with a topoisomerase I inhibitor, Ed-04, has shown clinical activity in ESCC in a phase 1b study. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of izalontamab brengitecan compared with chemotherapy in patients with advanced ESCC who progressed after first-line programmed cell death 1 protein (PD-1)/programmed cell death 1 ligand 1 (PD-L1) inhibitor plus platinum-containing chemotherapy. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This phase 3, open-label, randomized clinical trial was conducted across 80 hospitals in China. Patients with recurrent or metastatic ESCC that had progressed with first-line PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor plus platinum-containing chemotherapy were enrolled. Between March 19, 2024, and August 1, 2025 (final follow-up, October 17, 2025), a total of 704 patients were screened, and 497 were enrolled and randomized. INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either izalontamab brengitecan (n = 249; 2.5 mg/kg on days 1 and 8 every 3 weeks) or physician-selected chemotherapy (n = 248; irinotecan, paclitaxel, or docetaxel) every 3 weeks. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The dual primary end points were progression-free survival (PFS) assessed by blinded independent central review according to Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors version 1.1 and overall survival (OS). RESULTS: Of 497 patients who underwent randomization (median age, 61.0 years [range, 34-76]; 448 male patients [90.1%]), 493 received study treatment. At this interim analysis, izalontamab brengitecan demonstrated statistically significant improvement in both PFS and OS. Median PFS by blinded independent central review was 4.17 months (95% CI, 3.61-4.53 months) with izalontamab brengitecan vs 1.97 months (95% CI, 1.61-2.73 months) with chemotherapy (hazard ratio, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.40-0.63; log-rank P < .001). Median OS was 9.79 months (95% CI, 7.89-11.01 months) with izalontamab brengitecan vs 7.20 months (95% CI, 6.18-7.82 months) with chemotherapy (hazard ratio, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.48-0.82; log-rank P < .001). Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 212 of 249 patients (85.1%) with izalontamab brengitecan and 147 of 248 patients (59.3%) with chemotherapy and were predominantly hematologic. item.title: Disease Duration and Latent Symptom Phenotypes in Medically Refractory Chronic Rhinosinusitis.
item.dc:creator: Williams E, Minesinger K, Guevara G, Casiano RR, Palacio A, Levine CG
item.description:
Authors: Williams E, Minesinger K, Guevara G, Casiano RR, Palacio A, Levine CG
Journal: JAMA otolaryngology-- head & neck surgery | DOI: 10.1001/jamaoto.2026.3282
Published: 2026-Nov-12
PMID: 43018942



Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) symptom duration has not been associated with distinct patterns of symptom co-occurrence, limiting its utility for clinical phenotyping and treatment planning. Patients with longer-standing CRS may represent biologically or treatment-modified presentations, but it remains unclear whether symptom patterns differ systematically by duration. OBJECTIVE: To characterize symptom phenotypes based on CRS symptom duration and determine whether patterns of symptom co-occurrence differ systematically across duration categories. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: A cross-sectional analysis of prospectively collected data in a large CRS cohort including patients in academic tertiary care center rhinology clinics aged 11 to 85 years with CRS who in whom appropriate medical therapy was not successful, met criteria, and underwent endoscopic sinus surgery between January 1, 2020, and May 1, 2025. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Binary sinonasal symptom indicators from a structured symptom checklist were analyzed using multiple correspondence analysis (MCA) to identify latent patterns of symptom co-occurrence. Dimension scores were then compared across duration categories (<6 months, 6 months to 3 years, >3 years) using Kruskal-Wallis tests with post hoc Dunn testing. As convergent evidence, the 22-item Sino-Nasal Outcome Test (SNOT-22) total and subdomain scores were compared across the same duration groups. RESULTS: Among 661 patients (mean [SD] age, 54.4 [16.7] years; 364 [55.1%] male; 85 [12.9%] Black and 289 [43.7%] Hispanic), MCA of 21 binary sinonasal symptom indicators identified 3 principal dimensions, explaining 40% of total variance. Dimension 1 reflected global symptom burden and increased monotonically with symptom duration (ε2 = 0.035; 95% CI, 0.017-1.000). Dimension 2 captured a phenotypic shift between headache or pressure-dominant and chemosensory or drainage-dominant symptom patterns and varied across duration groups (ε2 = 0.025; 95% CI, 0.012-1.000). Dimension 3 captured airway-irritative and sensory features and varied across duration groups (ε2 = 0.019; 95% CI, 0.007-1.000), with post hoc testing showing separation between the 2 longer-duration groups. SNOT-22 total and subdomain scores replicated this threshold pattern across duration cohorts. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This study found that, in medically refractory CRS, the duration of symptoms was associated with structural differences in symptom phenotypes rather than simple, linear increases in symptom severity. Early chronic disease (<6 months) is characterized by a lower overall symptom burden and headache/pressure predominance. Longer disease duration is associated with greater total symptom load and a predominance of chemosensory dysfunction and drainage-dominant concerns. Additional longitudinal validation of these phenotypic patterns and their association with clinical response is needed.

item.title: Perivascular epithelial remodeling is reflected in circulating cfDNA methylation signals as detection markers for early esophageal tumorigenesis.
item.dc:creator: Yi Y, Li D, Zhang S, Bai Y, Lin Y, Liu Y, Ding Y, Feng C, He Z, Liu Q, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Yi Y, Li D, Zhang S, Bai Y, Lin Y, Liu Y, Ding Y, Feng C, He Z, Liu Q, et al.
Journal: Cancer discovery | DOI: 10.1158/2159-8290.CD-26-0691
Published: 2026-Nov-12
PMID: 43018467



Abstract:
Early detection of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is hindered by a lack of noninvasive biomarkers for precancerous lesions. Here, we report a circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation approach for early esophageal neoplasia detection. In prospective community screening, the assay achieved standardized sensitivity of 78% at 79% specificity for the clinically actionable endpoint of high-grade intraepithelial neoplasia (HGIN) or ESCC, with stage-specific sensitivities of 76% for HGIN and 86% for ESCC. Genome-wide methylation profiling reveals HGIN as an early epigenetic reprogramming stage. Integrative spatial and single-cell RNA sequencing reveals pronounced remodeling of the endothelial-proximal epithelial cell population, whose methylation signatures are detected in cfDNA. Guided by these findings, we develop an 11-gene cfDNA methylation panel that shows robust discrimination of early-stage ESCC across three retrospective case-control sets and an independent screening-derived case-control set. Together, these results demonstrate that our cfDNA methylation panel has promising utility for early ESCC detection.

item.title: Risk Factors for Osteoradionecrosis After Head and Neck Radiotherapy: A Systematic Review.
item.dc:creator: Le Guevelou J, Larnaudie A, Biau J, Chaux AG, Bourhis J, Pointreau Y
item.description:
Authors: Le Guevelou J, Larnaudie A, Biau J, Chaux AG, Bourhis J, Pointreau Y
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70546
Published: 2026-Nov-11
PMID: 43015994



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Although intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT) has led to a significant reduction in mandibular osteoradionecrosis (ORN) rates, head-and-neck radiotherapy (RT) is rapidly evolving-with increasing use of altered schedules and with novel systemic regimens including immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI). The aim of this work is to systematically review the established risk factors for ORN after head-and-neck RT and to provide a narrative outlook on emerging risk factors. MATERIAL AND METHODS: A systematic review of the literature was performed in September 2025 on three databases (PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase and Scopus), using the MeSH terms "osteoradionecrosis" and "head and neck neoplasm." No language restriction was applied. Studies deemed eligible were studies reporting factors associated with the onset of osteoradionecrosis after photon-based head-and-neck RT. RESULTS: A total of 14 articles were included (1 prospective, 13 retrospective). The proportion of patients who developed ORN ranged from 1.8% to 19.8%, with a median interval from RT to ORN onset of 8 to 40 months. Pre-RT dental extraction (particularly within 7 days before RT start) and higher mandibular dose-volume parameters (V50Gy, V60Gy, dose to the primary site) were consistently associated with ORN onset. Smoking was associated with a shorter time to ORN onset, and bone surgery with resection of the periosteum was a strong independent risk factor (HR 5.87). No included study reported altered fractionation (accelerated, hyperfractionated) as being a risk factor to develop ORN. CONCLUSION: Risk factors for ORN include both patient-related (smoking) and treatment-related (pre-RT dental extraction, mandibular V50Gy/V60Gy) parameters. Whether these risk factors retain their relevance in modern altered-fractionation schedules and in ICI-combination regimens is currently unknown and warrants dedicated analysis from prospective studies.

Abstract:
This phase Ib/II investigator-initiated, open label trial aims to show the safety and efficacy of Cystadane (betaine) in aspartylglucosaminuria, a lysosomal storage disorder characterized by progressive cognitive decline, in Finnish patients homozygous for the Finnish major mutation, aged between 3 and 17 years at study begin (recruited: 25, analyzed: 21). Oral Cystadane efficacy and safety were studied over 48 months. The primary endpoint of the study, reduction of glycoasparagines in the urine, was quantitatively determined using liquid chromatography/mass spectrometry and normalized to urine creatinine. Urine glycoasparagines are significantly reduced upon Cystadane treatment (by 68.6% ±10.8%; p = 0.000), and the study thus meets its primary endpoint. Our data show that Cystadane/betaine efficiently improves the main disease biomarker, and it is safe to use in aspartylglucosaminuria. item.title: Prognostic significance of minor versus major extranodal extension in oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.dc:creator: Vaira LA, Qadeer H, Lechien JR, Maniaci A, Maglitto F, Salzano G, Iannella G, Chiesa-Estomba CM, Boscolo-Rizzo P, De Riu G
item.description:
Authors: Vaira LA, Qadeer H, Lechien JR, Maniaci A, Maglitto F, Salzano G, Iannella G, Chiesa-Estomba CM, Boscolo-Rizzo P, De Riu G
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108220
Published: 2026-Nov-11
PMID: 43014091



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extranodal extension (ENE) is an established adverse prognostic factor in oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCSCC), but the clinical relevance of its extent remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the prognostic impact of quantitatively defined minor versus major ENE, with particular emphasis on the conventional 2-mm threshold. METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to August 2026. Studies of surgically treated OCSCC assessing pathological ENE extent and oncological outcomes were included. Random-effects meta-analyses using restricted maximum likelihood and Hartung-Knapp inference were performed when at least three compatible adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) were available. Risk of bias was assessed using QUIPS. RESULTS: Twenty-two reports representing 18 independent cohorts were included. Five studies contributed to the primary overall survival (OS) meta-analysis. Major ENE was associated with significantly worse OS than minor ENE (pooled HR 2.01, 95% CI 1.10-3.66; I2 = 60.5%). Three studies contributed to the disease-free survival (DFS) meta-analysis, showing a concordant but imprecise association (pooled HR 2.16, 95% CI 0.44-10.66; I2 = 59.3%). Alternative thresholds and morphological classifications also generally suggested poorer outcomes with increasing ENE extent. CONCLUSIONS: ENE extent provides prognostic information beyond binary ENE status in OCSCC. Major ENE is associated with worse OS, while evidence for DFS is directionally consistent but less precise. The 2-mm cutoff should be considered clinically useful but not yet biologically definitive.

item.title: Drought alters cowpea root endophytic fungal communities and functional characterization reveals plant growth-promoting potential of cultured endophytes.
item.dc:creator: Halo BA, Yaish MW
item.description:
Authors: Halo BA, Yaish MW
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360553
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43013566



Abstract:
Drought is a major constraint to cowpea productivity, but its effects on root-associated endophytic fungi remain poorly understood. This study investigated how drought influences cowpea root endophytic fungal communities and evaluated the plant growth-promoting potential of cultured fungal endophytes. Internal transcribed spacer (ITS) amplicon sequencing revealed that drought significantly altered fungal community composition. Several fungal taxa, including Aspergillus and Chaetomium, showed numerical differences in abundance under drought, although these taxon-specific differences were not significant after correction for multiple comparisons. In parallel, 13 fungal endophytes were isolated from drought-treated cowpea roots and evaluated for plant growth-promoting traits. The isolates differed in 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate (ACC) deaminase activity and presumptive indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) production, and several promoted wheat seedling growth under polyethylene glycol (PEG)-induced osmotic stress. Selected isolates also enhanced okra pollen germination under osmotic stress. Together, these findings demonstrate that drought alters the cowpea root endophytic fungal community and identify cultured endophytes with promising plant growth-promoting activities. Further evaluation through direct inoculation of cowpea under drought is needed to determine their potential for improving crop performance under water-limited conditions.

item.title: Computational evaluation of chromone-tetrazole hybrids as noncovalent inhibitors of SARS-CoV-2 Mpro.
item.dc:creator: Khibech O, Kadda S, Hammouti Y, Abadi S, Jodeh S, Hammouti B, Challioui A
item.description:
Authors: Khibech O, Kadda S, Hammouti Y, Abadi S, Jodeh S, Hammouti B, Challioui A
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0362385
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43013528



Abstract:
Emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants continue to demand orally tractable, non-covalent inhibitors of the conserved main protease (Mpro). Here, chromone-phenyl-tetrazole hybrids were prioritized using a multiscale computational strategy that connects drug-likeness, binding stability, free-energy ranking, conformational behavior, and quantum-level electronic features. The series showed favorable oral drug-like profiles and low-to-moderate predicted acute toxicity. Among the stable Mpro complexes, M2 displayed the strongest computed affinity (MM/GBSA ΔGbind = -38.8 kcal·mol ⁻ ¹), driven mainly by dispersion with limited desolvation cost, whereas M4 showed the most direct catalytic-dyad engagement through His41/Cys145-supported anchoring. DFT analysis rationalized these complementary profiles: M2 and M4 exhibited narrower HOMO-LUMO gaps (4.00 eV) and higher electronic softness, while ELF/NCI maps revealed heteroatom-centered electron reservoirs and weak intramolecular preorganization. The derived pharmacophore consists of a planar chromone π-platform bearing a carbonyl/phenolic acceptor-donor edge, a para-phenyl spacer for conjugation and hydrophobic occupancy, and a methoxy-tetrazole polar/π-rich head for Glu166/Phe140/His163 anchoring. Overall, M2 and M4 emerge as complementary lead chemotypes for experimental validation and structure-guided optimization against Mpro.

item.title: Piloting cannabis for sleep disturbance in palliative care over 5 weeks: The pillow study protocol.
item.dc:creator: Newton AM, Krok-Schoen JL, Stevens EE, Babalonis SL, Wagener TL, Hinton A, Benzo R, Brasky TM
item.description:
Authors: Newton AM, Krok-Schoen JL, Stevens EE, Babalonis SL, Wagener TL, Hinton A, Benzo R, Brasky TM
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361190
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43013521



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sleep disturbance affects 60% of cancer patients, 3-fold that of the general population, and is frequently driven by clinical characteristics, physical symptoms, and psychological distress. Sleep disturbance and other symptoms often exacerbate one another, leading to reduced health-related quality of life (HRQOL). Sleep is the most commonly reported reason for cannabis use among adults with cancer, yet clinical evidence supporting its use for symptom management remains limited. OBJECTIVES: This report describes a protocol for a pilot randomized trial designed to evaluate the safety and feasibility of a cannabis-based intervention and to explore its preliminary efficacy for sleep disturbance and HRQOL. METHODS: This pilot parallel-arm randomized clinical trial will enroll 50 patients from the Ohio State University Comprehensive Cancer Center (OSUCCC; anticipated Fall 2026). Eligible participants will be new to the OSUCCC's Palliative Care clinic and report at least moderate sleep disturbance. Participants will be randomized by sex and race strata to receive either usual care or a nightly oral cannabis gummy containing 5 mg Δ-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) and 5 mg cannabidiol (CBD), taken 1 hour before bedtime for 30 days. Adverse events will be monitored throughout the study. Sleep, HRQOL, and related symptoms will be assessed using self-reported questionnaires, ecological momentary assessments, and actigraphy. CONCLUSIONS: Findings will provide critical safety, feasibility, and preliminary efficacy data to support a future large-scale, multisite trial targeting sleep disturbance and symptom palliation in cancer care.

item.title: Targeting DHFR to suppress one-carbon metabolism and enhance radiation sensitivity in patients with NRF2-active head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Zolkind P, Wilkerson EM, Panda H, Chembo J, Sun J, Zhao K, Ley J, Atteberry M, Cho K, Wamsley NT, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Zolkind P, Wilkerson EM, Panda H, Chembo J, Sun J, Zhao K, Ley J, Atteberry M, Cho K, Wamsley NT, et al.
Journal: Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research | DOI: 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-26-0700
Published: 2026-Nov-11
PMID: 43013352



Abstract:
PURPOSE: NRF2 hyperactivity is associated with radiation resistance in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). We evaluated the dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) inhibitors pyrimethamine and its potent analog, WCDD115, as radiosensitizing agents through disruption of one-carbon metabolism. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Preclinical studies used NRF2-competent and deficient HNSCC models, clonogenic assays, transcriptomics, metabolomics, pharmacokinetics/toxicity testing, and syngeneic tumor grafts to assess WCDD115 as a novel radiosensitizing agent. In parallel, we conducted an open-label, single-center, window-of-opportunity early phase I clinical trial (NCT05678348) of previously untreated patients with HPV(-) stage III/IV HNSCC to receive pyrimethamine 50mg prior to surgery. Correlative analysis included mass spectrometry, western blotting, and pathway analysis. RESULTS: WCDD115 enhanced radiation-induced DNA damage and suppressed one-carbon metabolism and nucleotide biosynthesis. Parallel mouse tumor studies demonstrated that WCDD115 enhanced the efficacy of radiation in NRF2-competent but not NRF2-deficient tumors. In a clinical trial of neoadjuvant pyrimethamine, DHFR protein expression was enriched post-treatment by a mean fold change of 9.91 (95% confidence interval 8.1 to 12.2), consistent with a strong on-target effect. The drug was well tolerated with no drug-related grade 3-5 adverse events or surgical delays. CONCLUSIONS: NRF2 hyperactivity is associated with enhanced one-carbon metabolism which can be therapeutically targeted with DHFR inhibitors to promote radiation sensitization. In HNSCC patients, pyrimethamine achieves potent DHFR inhibition and a favorable safety profile supporting a future phase 2 trial integrating pyrimethamine with definitive radiation-based therapy for NRF2-active HNSCCs.

item.title: HOPO 14-1, an Oral Actinide Chelator: A Phase 1 Nonrandomized Clinical Trial.
item.dc:creator: Goonewardena SN, Atleski L, Bunin DI, Furimsky AM, Pui S, Green CE, Chang PY
item.description:
Authors: Goonewardena SN, Atleski L, Bunin DI, Furimsky AM, Pui S, Green CE, Chang PY
Journal: JAMA | DOI: 10.1001/jama.2026.19809
Published: 2026-Nov-11
PMID: 43013314



Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Current treatments approved by the US Food and Drug Administration for internal actinide contamination (pentetate calcium trisodium and pentetate zinc trisodium) require intravenous injection or nebulized inhalation under medical supervision and have limited radionuclide coverage. HOPO 14-1, an oral form of 3,4,3-LI(1,2-HOPO), is the first shelf-stable, broad-spectrum actinide chelator in clinical development that does not require intravenous access or trained personnel. In preclinical models, 3,4,3-LI(1,2-HOPO) removed a broad range of actinides, and its oral route supports scalable emergency medical use. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetic parameters, and excretion of a single dose of HOPO 14-1 in healthy adults. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a phase 1 nonrandomized clinical trial including 42 healthy adults (6 per dose level) with evaluations for 14 days after administration of a single dose and conducted at a single site in the US. Participants were recruited and screened between March 2023 and July 2025 and follow-up was completed in August 2025. INTERVENTION: Single oral dose of HOPO 14-1 administered at 1 of 7 dose levels (100 mg, 200 mg, 500 mg, 1200 mg, 2500 mg, 5000 mg, or 7500 mg) with follow-up through day 14 after dose administration. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcomes were the incidence and severity of adverse events, drug-related adverse events, and serious adverse events. The secondary outcomes were plasma pharmacokinetic parameters and cumulative urinary and fecal excretion. RESULTS: Of the 42 healthy adults enrolled (median age, 43 [IQR, 34-51] years; 64% female), all received a single dose of HOPO 14-1 (administered across all dose levels as assigned). There were no serious adverse events or dose-limiting toxic effects. The drug-related adverse events included diarrhea (31%), vomiting (14%), headache (12%), and fatigue (7%); all were mild to moderate in severity. Gastrointestinal adverse events were the principal tolerability findings and most evident at the highest doses. The plasma pharmacokinetic parameters demonstrated rapid absorption (median time of maximum plasma concentration, 0.86 [range, 0.53-1.60] hours to 1.90 [range, 1.40-2.90] hours) and dose-dependent increases in systemic exposure, with greater than proportional increases at higher doses. Fecal excretion was the primary route of elimination; urinary excretion was minimal. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Single oral doses of HOPO 14-1 up to 7500 mg were administered without dose-limiting toxicity or serious adverse events in healthy adults. Gastrointestinal tolerability defined the practical single-dose ceiling. These findings establish the first human safety and pharmacokinetic profile of a novel, orally administered actinide chelator and support further clinical evaluation of HOPO 14-1 as a countermeasure for internal radionuclide and heavy metal contamination. Development of a deployable and population-level emergency intervention addresses a long-standing unmet need with important implications for public health preparedness. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05628961.

item.title: Body composition and risks of head and neck cancers: evidence from a large-scale population-based cohort.
item.dc:creator: Li J, Li B, Qiu K, Deng D, Cheng D, Pang W, Song Y, Rao Y, Zhao Y, Ren J
item.description:
Authors: Li J, Li B, Qiu K, Deng D, Cheng D, Pang W, Song Y, Rao Y, Zhao Y, Ren J
Journal: Cancer causes & control : CCC | DOI: 10.1007/s10552-026-02281-7
Published: 2026-Nov-11

Abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to investigate the association between body compositions with overall/subtype-specific HNC risks. METHODS: We included participants from the UK Biobank with complete body composition data and without other cancers. Prospective analysis further excluded prevalent HNC. Multivariable logistic and Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to assess the associations. Subgroup analysis was stratified by age, sex, and smoking status. RESULTS: Among 399,640 participants included, 1,342 HNC cases were identified. Multiple body composition measures showed protective effects against overall HNC, including body mass index (BMI, overweight: odds ratio [OR] = 0.76, p < 0.001; obese: OR = 0.67, p < 0.001) and fat percentage of the whole-body (OR = 0.78, p < 0.001), trunk (OR = 0.81, p < 0.001), legs (OR = 0.74, p < 0.001), and arms (OR = 0.80, p < 0.001). Fat-free mass (FFM) of the whole-body (OR = 0.98, p < 0.001), trunk (OR = 0.95, p < 0.001), legs (OR = 0.88, p < 0.001) and arms (OR = 0.70, p < 0.001) also demonstrated protective effects. Additionally, site-specific body composition factors showed complex relationships with HNC subtypes and the prospective analysis confirmed most observed associations. CONCLUSION: BMI, fat percentage, and FFM were associated with lower risk of overall HNC, functioning mainly in males and old females.

item.title: Treatment Hotspots and Controversies in Papillary Thyroid Microcarcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Yu L, Liu F, Wang F, Yuan S, Zhao X, Gu S, Guo R, Zhao J, Zhang W
item.description:
Authors: Yu L, Liu F, Wang F, Yuan S, Zhao X, Gu S, Guo R, Zhao J, Zhang W
Journal: The oncologist | DOI: 10.1093/oncolo/oyag216
Published: 2026-Nov-10
PMID: 43010779



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The significant global rise in the detection rate of papillary thyroid microcarcinoma (PTMC) has sparked intense debates concerning overdiagnosis and overtreatment. Consequently, therapeutic strategies are shifting from radical surgery toward risk-stratified management, including active surveillance (AS) and minimally invasive techniques (MIT). Core controversies focus on the necessity of surgical intervention, the extent of prophylactic central neck dissection, and selection criteria for MIT versus conventional surgery. METHODS: This review systematically evaluates the comparative evidence on AS, thermal ablation (TA), and surgical treatment for PTMC, highlighting divergent Eastern and Western management philosophies to provide an optimized framework for clinical decision-making. RESULTS: Although AS demonstrates favorable survival benefits and health economic advantages for patients with PTMC, unresolved clinical risks persist. Notably, Chinese guidelines adopt stricter standards compared to the international 10 mm threshold. Among MIT, TA exhibits well-established short-term efficacy; however, recent expert consensus emphasizes a strict therapeutic hierarchy to prevent misuse, given the paucity of long-term recurrence data. CONCLUSION: An individualized framework based on risk stratification is essential for PTMC management, balancing oncological safety and quality of life.

item.title: Current Evidence of Precision Medicine via Multi-Omic Approaches in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma.

Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70544

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perioperative and adjuvant immunotherapy are new standards of care for selected patients with resectable locoregionally advanced HPV-negative HNSCC, but low pathologic response rates and a lack of predictive biomarkers limit patient selection and response-adapted care. This review examines multi-omic approaches to predicting immunotherapy response and personalizing therapy. METHODS: A narrative review of current multi-omic strategies for HNSCC was performed. Data providing predictive, prognostic, diagnostic, surveillance, or exploratory value was summarized. RESULTS: Multi-omics may identify those likely to benefit from immunotherapy. Single-cell transcriptomics reveals changes in the tumor immune microenvironment while spatial proteomics reveals tertiary lymphoid structures, dendritic cell networks, and protein signatures predicting immunotherapy response. Obstacles include unstandardized protocols, limited prospective validation, and small sample sizes. CONCLUSIONS: Multi-omics can reshape biomarker-driven HNSCC care, but implementation requires prospective validation, standardized protocols, and multi-platform integration.

item.title: Prognostic value of lymph node ratio beyond extranodal extension in node-positive oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Kumar A, Laskar SG, Sharma P, Sinha S, Mohanty S, Budrukkar A, Swain M, Pantvaidya G, Nair D, Thiagarajan S, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Kumar A, Laskar SG, Sharma P, Sinha S, Mohanty S, Budrukkar A, Swain M, Pantvaidya G, Nair D, Thiagarajan S, et al.
Journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.radonc.2026.111863
Published: 2026-Nov-10
PMID: 43008829



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Extranodal extension (ENE) is a key determinant of adjuvant therapy in node-positive oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCSCC). However, conventional nodal staging may not fully capture the quantitative burden of nodal disease. We evaluated whether lymph node ratio (LNR) provides additional prognostic value beyond ENE in a large randomized trial cohort. METHODS AND MATERIALS: We performed a retrospective subgroup analysis of 661 node-positive patients from the phase III randomized Oral Cavity Adjuvant Therapy (OCAT) trial. LNR was defined as the metastatic-to-dissected lymph node ratio and categorized as low (<0.10) or high (≥0.10). Overall survival (OS), recurrence-free survival (RFS), and locoregional control (LRC) were estimated using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression, adjusting for ENE, T stage, N stage, PNI, margin status, LVI, and treatment arm. RESULTS: With a median follow-up of 91 months, 387 deaths occurred. On multivariable analysis, high LNR remained independently associated with inferior OS (HR 1.43, 95% CI 1.15-1.78; p = 0.001), RFS (HR 1.48; p = 0.001), and LRC (HR 1.40; p = 0.018). High LNR/ENE-positive patients had significantly worse survival than the reference group, low LNR/ENE-negative (HR 2.08, 95% CI 1.47-2.95; p < 0.001). Low LNR/ENE-positive patients trended toward inferior survival (HR 1.36; p = 0.051), while high LNR/ENE-negative patients showed no significant difference (HR 1.12; p = 0.65). CONCLUSIONS: LNR is an independent prognostic factor beyond ENE across OS, RFS, and LRC in node-positive OCSCC. High LNR combined with ENE identifies a distinctly high-risk subgroup, whereas high LNR alone did not significantly impact survival in the absence of ENE. Incorporating LNR into postoperative risk stratification may refine identification of patients for risk-adapted adjuvant strategies.

item.title: A tumor biology-informed interpretation of TNM 9 in HPV-associated OPSCC.
item.dc:creator: Hoffmann M, Tribius S
item.description:
Authors: Hoffmann M, Tribius S
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108227
Published: 2026-Nov-10
PMID: 43008667



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 9th edition of the TNM classification (TNM-9) refines anatomical staging in head and neck cancer, maintaining p16-based categorization for HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC). However, anatomical extent alone does not capture key biological and host-related determinants of clinical behavior. METHODS: In this concept-driven synthesis, we integrate TNM-9 anatomy with evidence on transcriptional viral activity, p16 discordance, nodal morphology including imaging-defined extranodal extension (iENE), immune microenvironment, and host modifiers such as smoking and comorbidity. We propose a layered integrative framework that preserves TNM-9 structure while contextualizing tumor biology. The review is based on a selective synthesis of key translational and clinical studies identified through literature searches and expert knowledge, without a formal systematic approach. RESULTS: TNM-9 improves anatomical prognostic stratification at the population level, but identical anatomical stages encompass biologically heterogeneous entities. HPV RNA expression distinguishes biologically favorable tumors from p16+/HPV-inactive disease. iENE retains prognostic relevance in HPV-associated OPSCC, although its radiological appearance may partly reflect immune-associated stromal remodeling and cystic nodal morphology rather than invasive behavior alone. Smoking exposure, comorbidity burden, and immune-related host factors modify survival independent of tumor extent, explaining different outcomes within identical TNM stages. CONCLUSIONS: TNM-9 should be interpreted as an anatomical framework supplemented by biological and host factors. A multidimensional understanding enhances clinical applicability, avoids overtreatment of biologically favorable disease and highlights high-risk phenotypes concealed by anatomy alone. This perspective supports precise, biology-informed risk assessment in HPV-associated OPSCC. .

item.title: Treatment of Recurrent and/or Metastatic Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: CSCO and ASCO Joint Guideline.
item.dc:creator: Jiang W, Ismaila N, Chua ML, Haddad R, Le QT, Colevas AD, Saba NF, Harrington K, Huang SH, Chan AT, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Jiang W, Ismaila N, Chua ML, Haddad R, Le QT, Colevas AD, Saba NF, Harrington K, Huang SH, Chan AT, et al.
Journal: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology | DOI: 10.1200/JCO-26-02650
Published: 2026-Nov-10
PMID: 43008245



Abstract:
PURPOSE: To provide evidence-based recommendations on first- and subsequent-line systemic therapy, maintenance therapy, locoregional consolidation, and salvage local therapy for patients with recurrent and/or metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). METHODS: A multidisciplinary Expert Panel convened by CSCO and ASCO reviewed evidence from randomized trials, meta-analyses, systematic reviews, prospective and retrospective studies, and clinical experience. The guideline was informed by a systematic literature review and consensus-based interpretation of efficacy, safety, feasibility, and patient-centered outcomes across scenarios. Outcomes included overall and progression-free survival, response and disease control rates, toxicity, and quality of life. RESULTS: Evidence supports platinum-based chemotherapy plus a programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) inhibitor as preferred first-line therapy for medically fit patients. Evidence also supports maintenance strategies after disease control, while treatment selection depends on prior treatment, disease extent, patient fitness, resource availability, and preferences. Selected responders may receive locoregional consolidation radiotherapy or oral maintenance chemotherapy. For isolated locoregional recurrence amenable to local therapy, options include salvage surgery and re-irradiation. RECOMMENDATIONS: Chemotherapy plus a PD-1 inhibitor, followed by maintenance PD-1 inhibition for up to 2 years, should be offered first-line to appropriate patients with recurrent and/or metastatic NPC. Chemotherapy alone may be offered when immunotherapy is unsuitable or declined. Selected patients responding to first-line chemotherapy may receive oral maintenance chemotherapy or locoregional consolidation intensity-modulated radiotherapy. Salvage surgery or re-irradiation is recommended for appropriately selected patients with isolated locoregional recurrence. Subsequent-line options include chemotherapy, PD-1 inhibitors, and antibody-drug conjugates. Treatment should be individualized according to disease setting, prior therapy, expected toxicities, availability, local drug approvals, and patient preferences. Early supportive and specialist interdisciplinary palliative care, where available, should accompany active anticancer treatment for advanced, incurable disease.Additional information is available at www.ascopubs.org/topics/asco-guidelines/head-neck-cancer.

item.title: Treatment of Stage IB to III Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: CSCO-ASCO Guideline Update.
item.dc:creator: Chen YP, Ismaila N, Huang SH, Jiang W, Ma B, Haddad R, Le QT, Colevas AD, Harrington K, Yom SS, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Chen YP, Ismaila N, Huang SH, Jiang W, Ma B, Haddad R, Le QT, Colevas AD, Harrington K, Yom SS, et al.
Journal: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology | DOI: 10.1200/JCO-26-02648
Published: 2026-Nov-10
PMID: 43008242



Abstract:
PURPOSE: To update the 2021 CSCO-ASCO guideline on chemotherapy in combination with radiotherapy for the definitive treatment of non-metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), incorporating new evidence on radiotherapy techniques and target-volume de-escalation, chemotherapy regimens and their sequencing, adjuvant therapy, and immunotherapy for patients with stage IB-III disease. METHODS: A multidisciplinary Expert Panel reviewed evidence published since the prior guideline, including randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and relevant prospective and retrospective studies. Outcomes of interest included overall survival, failure-free or progression-free survival, locoregional and distant disease control, acute and late toxicities, and patient-reported quality of life. Recommendations were developed using the ASCO guideline development process and Expert Panel consensus. RESULTS: The updated evidence supports: IMRT with image guidance and MRI-based target delineation as core components of definitive treatment; selected response-adapted target delineation following induction chemotherapy; elective nodal de-escalation in appropriately selected patients; risk-adapted chemotherapy sequencing according to stage and biologic risk; cisplatin-based concurrent chemoradiotherapy; gemcitabine-cisplatin (GP) or docetaxel-cisplatin-fluorouracil (TPF) as preferred induction regimens; and selected adjuvant chemotherapy options, including metronomic capecitabine for patients with higher residual post-chemoradiotherapy risk. Several randomized trials evaluating PD-1 inhibitors have demonstrated improved disease-control outcomes, but overall survival data remain immature. RECOMMENDATIONS: This guideline update provides recommendations on radiotherapy technique, dose, imaging, and target delineation; sequencing of additional chemotherapy with radiotherapy; concurrent chemotherapy options; induction chemotherapy regimens and timing; adjuvant chemotherapy options; and the role of immunotherapy. At present, the Panel makes no recommendation for or against routine addition of immunotherapy to induction-concurrent chemoradiotherapy; applicability of the trial evidence, benefits and harms, local approval and access, and patient preferences should guide individualized decisions.Additional information is available at www.ascopubs.org/topics/asco-guidelines/head-neck-cancer.

item.title: Glycyrrhizinic Acid and Isatidis folium extracts combined with Bacillus subtilis protect against dextran sulfate sodi-um-induced colitis in Hu sheep.
item.dc:creator: Zheng D, Fu X, Li M, Liu Y, Liu D
item.description:
Authors: Zheng D, Fu X, Li M, Liu Y, Liu D
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0362464
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43008067



Abstract:
Weaning stress caused by maternal separation and dietary changes often leads to intestinal disorders such as diarrhea and enteritis in young animals, and the development of antibiotic-free, safe preparations to manage these conditions is therefore a promising strategy. The optimal proportion of each component in the formulation was determined in our preliminary study using orthogonal experimental design and range analysis. This study first evaluated the effects of glycyrrhizic acid and Isatidis folium extract on the growth of Bacillus subtilis (B. subtilis), and then examined the effects of the compound preparation (CP) composed of glycyrrhizic acid, Isatidis folium extract, and B. subtilis on in vitro antibacterial activity, growth performance, immune modulation, and the amelioration of dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis in Hu sheep. Twenty-seven 45-day-old healthy male Hu lambs (body weight = 15.83 ± 0.41 kg) were randomly assigned to 3 dietary groups, each dietary group consisted of 9 animals, were housed in 3 pens with 3 sheeps in each. The lambs were fed with the basal diets (control group), supplemented with 25 g (compound preparation group 1, CP1), 30 g (compound preparation group 2, CP2) CP per kg diet, respectively. Experimental design of protective effects of CP on lamb colitis was eighteen 45-days-old healthy male Hu lambs (body weight = 16.24 ± 0.86 kg) were randomly assigned to three groups (n = 6 per group), the lambs were fed with the basal diets (control group); lambs were fed with the basal diets for the first 7 days and were then given a single daily oral gavage of DSS at 4 g/kg body weight (DSS group); lambs were fed with the basal diet supplemented with 25 g CP per kg diet for the first 7 days and were then given a single daily oral gavage of DSS at 4 g/kg body weight (CP-DSS). The results showed that glycyrrhizic acid and Isatidis folium extract did not affect the growth of B. subtilis, while the CP significantly inhibited the growth of Escherichia coli (E. coli) and Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus). CP1 significantly increased daily weight gain; CP1 and CP2 significantly increased serum immunoglobulin G (IgG) and colonic mucosal secretory immunoglobulin A (SIgA) levels, as well as the relative mRNA expression of interferon γ (IFN-γ), interleukin-1β (IL-1β), interleukin-4 (IL-4), interleukin-6 (IL-6) and interleukin-10 (IL-10). Supplementation with 25 g CP per kg diet significantly downregulated the relative mRNA expression of proinflammatory cytokines (IFN-γ, IL-1β, IL-6) and upregulated the relative mRNA expression of anti-inflammatory cytokines (IL-4, IL-10) and intestinal barrier factors (ZO-1, occludin, Muc2, α-catenin), alleviating colonic damage. These findings support its potential as a safe and effective feed additives for promoting intestinal health in sheep.

item.title: Prevalence of human papillomavirus and HPV vaccination among cisgender bisexual women: Protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.dc:creator: Lawley KA, Kusuma K, Farquhar SA, Goodreau SM, Winer RL
item.description:
Authors: Lawley KA, Kusuma K, Farquhar SA, Goodreau SM, Winer RL
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360427
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43008003



Abstract:
Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the most common sexually transmitted infection in the United States, and a primary cause of cervical cancer. Although cervical cancer is largely preventable through HPV vaccination, vaccine coverage remains suboptimal. Research on HPV prevalence and vaccination among cisgender bisexual women is limited and inconsistent. This may be partly due to variation in how bisexuality is defined. Bisexuality may be operationalized based on sexual identity (e.g., self-identification as bisexual) or sexual behavior (e.g., sexual contact with more than one sex or gender), and these differing definitions may capture distinct populations and yield divergent health findings. This paper proposes a protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis to examine whether reported HPV prevalence and vaccination rates among cisgender bisexual women differ based on whether bisexuality is defined by identity or behavior. The protocol is registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251252015) and follows PRISMA-P guidelines. Random-effects meta-analyses will estimate pooled HPV prevalence and vaccination rates by definition type. Findings will clarify how operational definitions shape observed HPV-related outcomes and inform tailored cervical cancer prevention strategies for cisgender bisexual women.

item.title: Lymphopenia and Circulating Biomarker Dynamics Associated with Clinical Outcome and Toxicity in Pazopanib-Treated Radioiodine-Refractory Thyroid Cancer: Exploratory Analyses from the Pazothyr Trial.
item.dc:creator: Rodriguez C, Dalban C, Colombe-Vermorel A, Odeyer L, Lamartina L, Godbert Y, Illouz F, Gautier J, Treilleux I, Darnis S, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Rodriguez C, Dalban C, Colombe-Vermorel A, Odeyer L, Lamartina L, Godbert Y, Illouz F, Gautier J, Treilleux I, Darnis S, et al.
Journal: Thyroid : official journal of the American Thyroid Association | DOI: 10.1177/10507256261500974
Published: 2026-Nov-10
PMID: 43007078



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pazopanib showed clinical activity in progressive radioiodine-refractory differentiated thyroid carcinoma (RAIR-DTC), although its use is limited by substantial toxicity not reduced by intermittent treatment. We aimed to identify biomarkers associated with outcome and treatment-related toxicity in these patients. METHODS: This study reported exploratory results related to the Pazothyr trial (NCT01813136) investigating pazopanib efficacy in RAIR-DTC patients. We evaluated lymphopenia and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) from the Pazothyr clinical database (n = 168). Dedicated informed consent for additional plasma and tumor sample collection allowed quantification of plasma angiogenic factors and cytokines at baseline and after one month of pazopanib (n = 111). Immune markers (CD8, FOXP3, CD163, and PDL1) analyzed by immunohistochemistry in archived primary tumors from patients (n = 68) with response or stable disease after 6 months of pazopanib were scored semiquantitatively. Associations with response, progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and substantial treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were evaluated. Given the exploratory nature of this study, no adjustment for multiple comparisons was performed. RESULTS: At baseline, moderate and severe lymphopenia were associated with shorter PFS, unlike high NLR. Elevated Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor A (VEGF-A), Interleukin 6 (IL-6), and CXCL8 correlated with poorer PFS. High VEGF-A, hepatocyte growth factor (HGF), IL-6, CXCL8, and CXCL9 were associated with shorter OS. X Early changes in placental growth factor (PlGF), HGF, interleukin 12 subunit p40, and CXCL10 were associated with substantial TRAEs. Multivariable analyses identified baseline severe lymphopenia (hazard ratio [HR] = 2.39 [confidence interval or CI 1.27-4.48], p = 0.007) and high CXCL8 (HR = 2.01 [CI 1.26-3.21], p = 0.004) as independent factors associated with progression. High baseline NLR (HR = 2.26 [CI 1.21-4.22], p = 0.01), HGF (HR = 2.37 [CI 1.33-4.20], p = 0.003), and CXCL8 (HR = 2.20 [CI 1.25-3.87], p = 0.006) were similarly associated with death. One-month increases in PlGF (odds ratio [OR] = 2.49 [CI 1.13-5.50], p = 0.024) and HGF (OR = 2.91 [CI 1.32-6.43], p = 0.008) were independently associated with substantial TRAEs. In patients with tumor samples, Programmed cell Death-Ligand 1 (PDL1)-immune cell score (ICS) >1% (HR = 2.05 [CI 1.15-3.66], p = 0.015) was also associated with progression. CONCLUSIONS: Baseline lymphopenia and inflammatory plasma biomarkers were associated with clinical outcome, whereas early changes in circulating factors were associated with substantial TRAEs. These exploratory results require prospective validation in RAIR-DTC patients treated with pazopanib or other VEGF receptor-targeting multikinase inhibitors. The relevance of PDL1-ICS expression for anti-PD1/PDL1-based therapies requires dedicated prospective trials.

item.title: Isolated Cephalic Perfusion via Aortic Occlusion for Cervicofacial Simulation: Validation of a High-Fidelity Cadaveric Model.

item.description:

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: High-fidelity simulation may improve surgical training in head and neck surgery, yet validated perfused cadaveric models remain scarce. We evaluated the face, content, and construct validity of a perfused cadaveric model using isolated cephalic perfusion for cervicofacial surgical simulation. STUDY DESIGN: Prospective validation study of a reperfused cadaveric model using SIMLIFE® technology. SETTING: Institute of Anatomy and Surgical Simulation, Toulouse University Hospital. METHODS: Twenty unilateral levels I to IV neck dissections were performed on 11 body donors using a perfused SIMLIFE® model with isolated cephalic perfusion. Seven experts and 5 residents participated. Face and content validity were assessed using Likert-scale questionnaires, whereas construct validity was evaluated using the Onco-Neck-Score through blinded video assessment. RESULTS: High face validity was demonstrated across most assessed domains, particularly venous wall consistency, venous coloration, nerve appearance, and bleeding flow following vascular injury. Experts rated the model as highly relevant for resident training and surgical skills acquisition.
