It provides a realistic environment for neck dissection simulation and may represent a promising tool for surgical education and competency assessment.

item.title: Bioactive Peptide HX-12C Ameliorates Oral Submucous Fibrosis via Inhibition of TGF-β/Smad-Driven Myofibroblast Activation: A Potential Therapeutic Strategy.
item.dc:creator: Huang W, Shi R, Wang Y, Wang X, Qin Z, Luo X, Li K, Wang B, Hu Y
item.description:
Authors: Huang W, Shi R, Wang Y, Wang X, Qin Z, Luo X, Li K, Wang B, Hu Y
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70569
Published: 2026-Nov-10
PMID: 43006167



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the anti-fibrotic effects and mechanism of action of the bioactive peptide HX-12C in oral submucous fibrosis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Primary human buccal mucosal fibroblasts were treated with arecoline to induce a myofibroblast phenotype. The effects of HX-12C on cell proliferation, migration and fibrotic markers were assessed. Molecular docking and immunofluorescence were used to examine HX-12C binding to transforming growth factor-beta receptor I, validated by the inhibitor SB-431542. In vivo efficacy was evaluated in a bleomycin-induced rat model of oral submucous fibrosis. RESULTS: HX-12C promoted fibroblast proliferation and migration but suppressed arecoline-induced myofibroblast activation, downregulating alpha-smooth muscle actin, fibronectin and collagens I/III. Mechanistically, HX-12C bound to transforming growth factor-beta receptor I, inhibited SMAD2/3 phosphorylation and downstream pro-fibrotic gene expression, effects attenuated by SB-431542. In vivo, HX-12C improved mouth opening and reduced collagen deposition. CONCLUSIONS: HX-12C exerts potent anti-fibrotic effects by directly targeting transforming growth factor-beta receptor I and inhibiting the canonical transforming growth factor-beta/Smad signalling pathway. Our findings identify HX-12C as a promising therapeutic candidate for oral submucous fibrosis and provide a rationale for developing peptide-based therapies for transforming growth factor-beta-driven fibrotic diseases.

item.title: Betel-Quid Exposure and Site-Specific Prognostic Patterns in Oral Cavity Squamous Cell Carcinoma.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Betel-quid chewing is a risk factor for oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCSCC), but its associations with tumour subsite and depth-of-invasion (DOI) related prognosis remain unclear. We examined site-specific associations and exposure-stratified DOI thresholds for disease-specific survival (DSS). METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 454 patients from southern Thailand. Tumour-subsite associations were assessed using multivariable logistic regression. Exploratory DSS thresholds were derived among surgically treated patients using maximally selected log-rank statistics and evaluated with an exposure-stratified Cox model. RESULTS: Of 454 patients, 154 (33.9%) were betel chewers. Exposure was associated with tumours of the buccal mucosa (adjusted odds ratio, 5.43), lip (3.96), retromolar trigone (3.28) and gingiva (3.13), relative to oral tongue tumours. Exploratory DOI thresholds were 7 mm in chewers (log-rank p = 0.006) and 15 mm in non-chewers (p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Betel-quid exposure was associated with OCSCC at quid-contact subsites. Chewers showed a lower exploratory DOI threshold for DSS than non-chewers.

Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70564
Published: 2026-Nov-10

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Injectable platelet-rich fibrin (i-PRF) is increasingly used for articular temporomandibular disorders (TMD), but it is unclear whether randomised controlled trials (RCTs) report validated diagnostic criteria for participant enrolment. This scoping review maps the diagnostic instruments reported in i-PRF RCTs for articular TMD. It does not assess whether diagnostic systems were applied correctly or the accuracy of diagnoses. METHODS: Following the JBI framework and PRISMA-ScR, RCTs evaluating i-PRF for articular TMD and reporting pain and/or maximum mouth opening were searched in six databases, without date or language restrictions, plus grey literature, trial registries and reference lists. Diagnostic approaches, sample characteristics, imaging, interventions, comparators, follow-up and adverse events were charted. RESULTS: Thirteen RCTs were included. Five reported Wilkes staging, three reported imaging without a clinical diagnostic system, and two reported no diagnostic criterion. No trial reported RDC/TMD. CONCLUSION: Fewer than a quarter of i-PRF RCTs reported enrolment using a currently validated diagnostic system. This methodological finding does not indicate whether i-PRF is effective. Future trials should use DC/TMD and report diagnostic procedures in full.

item.title: Early Chidamide Maintenance After Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation in High-Risk Myeloid Malignancies: A Prospective Cohort With Time-Dependent External-Control Analysis.

item.title: TTA-MVUM: A Tumor and Text-Aware Multi-View Mamba Framework for Clinical Target Volume Auto-Segmentation in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma Radiotherapy.

item.description:
Authors: Ma X, Wu R, Yi J, Dai J, Men K
Journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics | DOI: 10.1016/j.ijrobp.2026.10.035
Published: 2026-Nov-09

Abstract:
PURPOSE: Accurate segmentation of clinical target volumes (CTV) is critical for the success of radiotherapy in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). Manual contouring is time-consuming and prone to considerable inter-observer variability. Current auto-segmentation models rely exclusively on images, which may lead to sub-optimal accuracy. This study sought to substantially improve CTV auto-segmentation by incorporating tumor and clinical text information with multimodal deep learning. METHODS AND MATERIALS: We retrospectively collected data from 184 NPC patients treated at our institution, with 144 cases allocated for model training and 40 for test. We propose a tumor- and text-aware multi-view UMamba (TTA-MVUM) model with text-image cross-attention modules to fuse visual and textual features. The model input comprised CT images, manually contoured primary gross tumor volume and metastatic lymph nodes, structured text contouring plan extracted by a large language model from electronic health records. Training was guided by a composite loss integrating Dice, cross-entropy and contrastive terms. Model performance was evaluated using Dice, 95% Hausdorff distance and averaged surface distance. RESULTS: The proposed TTA-MVUM model significantly outperformed state-of-the-art image-only and tumor-aware baselines, yielding mean Dice of 0.892 ± 0.035 for high-risk CTV, 0.738 ± 0.149 for low-risk CTV, and 0.889 ± 0.024 for the entire CTV, respectively, with similar improvements for other metrics. CONCLUSIONS: Integrating tumor priors and text guidance can substantially improve the NPC CTV auto-segmentation accuracy and clinical applicability.

item.title: Prognostic value of pre-treatment nodal appearance, volume and kinetics in High-Risk non-HPV related oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma.

Abstract:
PURPOSE: We investigated the risk and prognostic value of pre-treatment nodal progression to inform the safe de-escalation of elective nodal irradiation (ENI) in high-risk oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC). METHODS: We identified patients with p16-negative, clinical T4, node-positive OPSCC treated consecutively with definitive radiotherapy between 2008 and 2021 from a prospectively maintained database. Association of nodal factors and oncologic outcomes were assessed using regression models. RESULTS: A total of 79 patients with a median 30-day interval between diagnostic and simulation scan were identified. Nodal growth was minimal with a median absolute change of + 0.5 cc and growth rate of 0.3%/day. Nodal kinetics and duration between imaging were not prognostic for treatment response. While no patients developed de novo pathological nodal disease, 14% of patients had indeterminant nodes on diagnostic scan, with 27% of these becoming pathological at time of simulation. While lack of new nodal disease and minimal growth over a 30-day pre-treatment interval supports the investigation of novel timing of ENI, particular care should be taken in patients to identify and appropriately manage indeterminate nodes at risk for progression.

item.title: A prospective comparative evaluation of dysphagia in surgically resected oral cavity cancers treated by dysphagia optimized volumetric modulated arc therapy (DO-VMAT) versus standard volumetric modulated arc therapy (S-VMAT): DECODE trial.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radiotherapy induced dysphagia is a common side effect in post-operative oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCSCC) patients, affecting quality of life (QOL). Dysphagia-optimized radiotherapy reduces dose to dysphagia aspiration-related structures (DARS) while maintaining oncological efficacy. Abstract:
PURPOSE: MAPK pathway activation suppresses iodine-handling genes, including sodium-iodide symporter (NIS), contributing to loss of iodine avidity in radioiodine-refractory thyroid cancer. Abstract:

item.description:
Authors: Miri M, Lechien JR

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To synthesize the current evidence on the histological architecture and biochemical composition of the healthy human vocal fold, and to critically appraise how phonotrauma alters these structural and molecular components. METHODS: Two independent investigators conducted a comprehensive narrative literature search of PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane databases, using MeSH and free-text terms related to vocal fold histology, biochemistry, and phonotrauma. Studies investigating histological, ultrastructural, or molecular modifications of the vocal folds, across human, animal, ex vivo, and cell-line models, were considered eligible. RESULTS: The healthy vocal fold exhibits a multilayered architecture comprising a non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium, a basement membrane, and a three-layered lamina propria, with the maculae flavae anchoring the membranous portion at its anterior and posterior insertions. Epithelial barrier integrity is maintained by tight junctions (occludin, ZO-1/2/3, claudins) and adherens junctions (E-cadherin, catenins), while surface hydration is regulated by transepithelial ion transport (Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase, NKCC1, ENaC, CFTR, TMEM16A) and aquaporin channels (AQP3, AQP4, AQP5). The lamina propria displays a stratified composition of collagen (≈ 43% of total protein), elastin (≈ 9%), hyaluronic acid, sulfated glycosaminoglycans, proteoglycans (decorin, fibromodulin, versican), and glycoproteins (fibronectin), which collectively determine the viscoelastic properties of the cover. Phonotrauma induces epithelial desquamation, microhole formation, downregulation of tight-junction proteins (occludin, ZO-1, E-cadherin), basement membrane thickening, upregulation of inflammatory mediators (IL-1β, TNF-α, COX-2, MMP-8), and progressive remodeling of the extracellular matrix, with species- and time-dependent alterations of fibronectin, decorin, fibromodulin, hyaluronic acid, and collagen subtypes. CONCLUSION: Phonotrauma triggers a coordinated cascade of histological, ultrastructural, cellular, and molecular alterations that disrupt the highly specialized architecture and viscoelastic properties of the vocal fold cover. A comprehensive understanding of these phonotrauma-induced changes is essential to inform preventive strategies, optimize voice therapy approaches, and guide future tissue-engineering and regenerative interventions for voice disorders.

Abstract:

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Primary sinonasal extraskeletal Ewing sarcoma (EES) is exceedingly rare, and its clinical characteristics and outcomes remain poorly characterized. We review regulatory reform and the 2015 to 2025 evolution of clinical development across small molecules, mAbs, multispecific antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates, and cell and gene therapies. China's disease burden and enrollment capacity have enabled globally relevant advances in EGFR-mutant lung cancer, gastrointestinal malignancies, hepatocellular carcinoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, and CLDN18.2-directed therapies. We highlight persistent challenges in target and modality convergence, biomarker definition, therapeutic window optimization, manufacturing consistency, and globally interpretable evidence generation and discuss how artificial intelligence may connect target discovery, drug design, and clinical trial optimization more efficiently. SIGNIFICANCE: China has become a major source of oncology trials and modality innovation, but scale alone will not ensure global impact. This review links regulatory reform, disease-specific opportunity, target biology, therapeutic format, and evidence quality across a decade of solid tumor development. It defines the conditions under which China-originated programs can generate globally practice-changing evidence. See related article by Shi, p. XX .

item.title: Cangrelor versus crushed ticagrelor in acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (DAPT-SHOCK-AMI): a randomised, double-blind trial.

Published: 2026-Nov-07
PMID: 42998670



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) can compromise the administration and absorption of oral P2Y12 inhibitors and carries high ischaemic and mortality risks. This trial assessed whether intravenous cangrelor was non-inferior to crushed oral ticagrelor for short-term clinical outcomes and whether it provided faster and more consistent platelet inhibition in patients with AMI-CS. METHODS: DAPT-SHOCK-AMI was a double-blind trial conducted at 29 hospitals across five European countries (Czech Republic, France, Germany, Poland, and Slovakia). Patients older than 18 years with AMI-CS were randomly assigned (1:1 ratio, stratified by centre, age, sex, presence or absence of ST-segment elevation, and mechanical ventilation) to cangrelor (30 μg/kg bolus followed by an infusion of 4 μg/kg per min for at least 2 h) or crushed ticagrelor (180 mg loading dose). The primary laboratory endpoint was a platelet reactivity index of less than 50% at the end of primary percutaneous coronary intervention. The primary clinical endpoint was death, myocardial infarction, or ischaemic stroke at 30 days. The primary clinical endpoint was analysed for non-inferiority with a prespecified margin of 1 percentage point among all randomly assigned patients who received study treatment. The study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03551964) and EudraCT (2018-002161-19); recruitment and 1-year follow-up are complete, and 5-year follow-up is ongoing. FINDINGS: Between Aug 1, 2018, and Jan 19, 2024, 605 patients (137 [23%] were female) were randomly assigned to cangrelor (n=298) or ticagrelor (n=307); no surviving patients were lost to the 1-year follow-up. The primary laboratory endpoint was analysed in 56 (19%) patients in the cangrelor group and 68 (22%) in the ticagrelor group, and was achieved in 56 (100%) of 56 patients receiving cangrelor and 15 (22%) of 68 receiving ticagrelor (p<0·0001). The 30-day primary clinical endpoint occurred in 112 (38%) of 298 patients receiving cangrelor and 126 (41%) of 307 receiving ticagrelor; non-inferiority was not demonstrated (difference -4 percentage points [90% CI -10 to 3]; Pnon-inferiority=0·13). Major bleeding at 30 days occurred in 19 (6%) of 298 patients receiving cangrelor and 16 (5%) of 307 receiving ticagrelor. INTERPRETATION: To our knowledge, this is the first randomised trial to compare P2Y12 inhibitor strategies specifically in patients with AMI-CS. Cangrelor achieved effective platelet inhibition more frequently than crushed ticagrelor at the end of primary percutaneous coronary intervention. Non-inferiority of cangrelor versus crushed ticagrelor was not demonstrated for the primary 30-day clinical endpoint. These trial findings can inform future trials of P2Y12 inhibition strategies in patients with AMI-CS. item.title: Global Proposal for the TNM Staging System for Poorly Differentiated Thyroid Cancer.
item.dc:creator: Shi X, Liu Q, Scholfield D, Li D, Lamartina L, Chen S, Zhang H, Papachristos AJ, Hamdy O, Timofeeva N, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Shi X, Liu Q, Scholfield D, Li D, Lamartina L, Chen S, Zhang H, Papachristos AJ, Hamdy O, Timofeeva N, et al.
Journal: JAMA oncology | DOI: 10.1001/jamaoncol.2026.4705
Published: 2026-Nov-06
PMID: 42994809



Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Poorly differentiated thyroid cancer (PDTC) lacks a dedicated staging system, requiring use of the eighth version of the American Joint Committee on Cancer and Union for International Cancer Control TNM staging system (TNM-8) for differentiated thyroid cancer despite its distinct biology. OBJECTIVE: To develop a PDTC-specific staging system. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study analyzed data from the International Aggressive Thyroid Cancer Collaborative Group (IATCCG), including surgically treated patients at 91 centers in 14 countries from January 1984 to January 2026. External validation was performed using patients from the US Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database. Data were analyzed from December 2025 to June 2026. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point was overall survival. With M1 disease predefined as stage IVB, the schema for stages I-IVA in patients with M0 disease were redefined. All possible TN combinations were fitted into multivariable Cox models, with the lowest Akaike information criterion defining the proposed system. Prognostic discrimination was assessed using adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) and C statistics. RESULTS: Among 1010 patients in the IATCCG cohort, 610 (60.4%) were female, and the median (IQR) age at diagnosis was 58 (46-68) years; median (IQR) follow-up was 41 (15-85) months. Among 170 patients in the SEER cohort, 85 (50.0%) were female, and the median (IQR) age at diagnosis was 61 (49-72) years; median (IQR) follow-up was 92 (42-154) months. In the IATCCG cohort, level VII lymph node metastasis (LNM) was associated with lower 5-year overall survival (45.2%; 95% CI, 33.4-61.2) than level VI (73.2%; 95% CI, 64.4-83.3) or lateral neck LNM (56.7%; 95% CI, 49.4-65.0). Level VII LNM was therefore reclassified from N1a to N1c. The lowest Akaike information criterion configuration among 16 738 candidates defined stages I to IVA as follows: I, T1N0/NX/N1a or T2N0/NX; II, T1N1b/N1c, T2N1a/N1b, or T3N0/NX/N1a; III, T2N1c, T3N1b, or T4aN0/NX/N1a; IVA, T3N1c, T4aN1b/N1c, or T4b any N; and IVB, M1 disease. Compared with TNM-8, stage I disease decreased from 44.4% (448 of 1010) to 24.6% (248 of 1010) and stage IV disease increased from 18.5% (187 of 1010) to 32.4% (327 of 1010) with the proposed system. The proposed staging had a higher C statistic than TNM-8 (0.74 [95% CI, 0.71-0.76] vs 0.71 [95% CI, 0.68-0.74]; difference, 0.03; 95% CI, 0.01-0.04). Corresponding SEER C statistic values were 0.76 (95% CI, 0.71-0.81) vs 0.74 (95% CI, 0.68-0.79), respectively (difference, 0.02; 95% CI, -0.01 to 0.06). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This cohort study found that this PDTC-specific staging system provides improved prognostic stratification reflecting its different biology. These data provide a strong rationale for the potential inclusion of a stand-alone American Joint Committee on Cancer staging system for PDTC.

item.title: Evaluation of the efficacy of Si-based agent in Rheumatoid Arthritis with complicating vestibular impairment.
item.dc:creator: Harada S, Koyama Y, Kobayashi Y, Imai T, Yoshioka Y, Kobayashi H, Inohara H, Shimada S
item.description:
Authors: Harada S, Koyama Y, Kobayashi Y, Imai T, Yoshioka Y, Kobayashi H, Inohara H, Shimada S
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361954
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42993734



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by persistent joint inflammation and progressive disability. Although current therapies have improved clinical outcomes, safer and more effective therapeutic approaches remain needed. Silicon (Si)-based agents have antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties and have shown beneficial effects in several inflammatory disease models. METHODS: We evaluated the effects of oral administration of a Si-based agent in a type II collagen-induced arthritis mouse model. Arthritis severity was assessed using an arthritis index, hindlimb oedema, and the hindlimb extension reflex test. Serum type II collagen-specific autoantibody levels were also measured. Vestibular function was evaluated using the vestibulo-ocular reflex (VOR), and inner-ear structural changes were assessed by magnetic resonance imaging and histological analysis. RESULTS: The Si-based agent reduced arthritis-related outcomes, including the arthritis index, hindlimb oedema, and joint movement restriction, and reduced serum type II collagen-specific autoantibody levels. In contrast, no significant differences between the Si-based agent and control groups were detected in VOR-related outcomes, endolymphatic space measurements, or inner-ear histological findings. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that the Si-based agent may have beneficial effects on arthritis-related manifestations. However, its effects on the vestibular function-related outcomes examined in this study were not evident. Further studies are needed to clarify the relationship between RA and vestibular dysfunction and to determine the potential therapeutic effects of Si-based agent on these complications.

item.title: Protocol for investigating the association between Helicobacter pylori exposure, antigen-specific serological responses, and resistant versus non-resistant hypertension in a South African cohort.
item.dc:creator: Mennen MC, Zulu MZ, Mabatha KC, Baguma R, Skelem S, Mbundwini NN, Aremu OO, Adriaanse M, van Dijk D, Pillay P, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Mennen MC, Zulu MZ, Mabatha KC, Baguma R, Skelem S, Mbundwini NN, Aremu OO, Adriaanse M, van Dijk D, Pillay P, et al.
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0362215
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42993715



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a leading contributor to cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, with poor control in low- and middle-income countries. Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) has been associated with hypertension through inflammatory, endothelial, metabolic and immune pathways, but data from sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in resistant hypertension, are limited. METHODS: This cross-sectional observational study will enrol 200 adults aged ≥18 at a tertiary academic hospital in Cape Town, South Africa: 80 with resistant hypertension, 80 with non-resistant hypertension and 40 with normotension. Participants will undergo standardised clinical assessment, blood pressure measurement, and collection of blood, urine and saliva. H. pylori exposure will be assessed using the Pylori DuoTect® point-of-care assay, which detects antibodies to CagA and FliD. Laboratory analyses will include lipid profile, inflammatory and nitric oxide-related markers, homocysteine, insulin indices, complete blood count, ghrelin, multiplex cytokine profiling and flow cytometric immunophenotyping. PAXgene® blood RNA samples will be retained for future exploratory analyses. Saliva will undergo exploratory H. pylori antigen testing using CerTest® kits, which are validated for stool rather than saliva. Saliva analysis will be exploratory, and results will not define the primary H. pylori exposure variable. Remaining saliva will be kept for potential future oral microbiome analyses not defined in this protocol. Multivariable logistic regression will evaluate associations between H. pylori exposure and hypertension phenotype, adjusting for demographic, lifestyle, and clinical covariates. DISCUSSION: To our knowledge, this will be the first African study to integrate point-of-care H. pylori serology with detailed clinical, inflammatory, metabolic, and immunological profiling across resistant hypertension, non-resistant hypertension and normotension. Findings may clarify biological pathways linking H. pylori exposure to blood pressure dysregulation and inform future mechanistic and interventional studies.

item.title: A systematic review of Moringa oleifera seed toxicity and safety: Comparative analysis of toxicology methodologies and results.
item.dc:creator: Russell JJ, Pritchard M, Paterson AWJ
item.description:
Authors: Russell JJ, Pritchard M, Paterson AWJ
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360006
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42993711



Abstract:
This systematic review aims to assess the reliability of contemporary toxicological research on Moringa oleifera seeds. Academic databases were browsed on a yearly basis (2014-2024); identification and screening were conducted between July 17th 2023 and January 13th 2025. Primary research reports on M. oleifera seed toxicology were included for data collection. Fifty-three fields were used to collect data. Data was synthesised by comparing methodological data points to contemporary toxicity testing guidelines; results were presented as a narrative synthesis. Conflict of interest, research quality and risk of bias were assessed using Cochrane tools modified for non-human laboratory studies. Thirty-seven non-duplicate publications were identified, of which 14 were included for data collection. In total, 395 data points were collected and synthesised. Financial conflicts of interest were declared in one report. Nine reports received "lower quality" or "lowest quality" research quality judgements. Six reports received "high risk of bias" judgements. Bias risk was commonly associated with selective reporting of data. M. oleifera seed toxicity was commonly tested via rodent study. Seven rodent studies included an acute toxicity test and nine included a sub-acute toxicity test. Two acute oral toxicity tests returned LD50 values of 14,000-15,000 mg/kg bw. Three sub-acute oral toxicity tests returned NOAEL values of 100-257 mg/kg bw/d. Oral LD50 and NOAEL data could only be derived from reports with "lowest quality" research and/or "high risk of bias" judgements, so these safety limits are unreliable. Inadequate dosing schemes were the primary cause of limited LD50 and NOAEL data. Dose range non-compliance also caused unnecessary animal suffering. To facilitate standardisation in future research, several guideline-based methodological recommendations are made. Determining reliable safety limits for M. oleifera seed consumption may reduce incidence of acute kidney injury, thereby supporting Targets 3.4 and 3.d of the United Nations sustainable development goals.

item.title: Testing the effects of nicotine concentration and nicotine source claims on oral nicotine pouch packaging engagement, self-reported perceptions and use intentions, and product trial in young adults and adults: Protocol for a randomized trial.
item.dc:creator: Long L, Alalwan MA, Alvarado E, Kozar A, Stevens EM, Shang C, Roberts ME, Klein EG, Shoben A, Mays D
item.description:
Authors: Long L, Alalwan MA, Alvarado E, Kozar A, Stevens EM, Shang C, Roberts ME, Klein EG, Shoben A, Mays D
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0362172
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42993708



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oral nicotine pouches (ONPs) are novel nicotine products and evidence on how features of ONP packaging affect product engagement, perceptions, use intentions, and behavior is limited. OBJECTIVES: We outline the protocol for a randomized trial examining how nicotine concentration and nicotine source claims affect engagement with ONP packaging using psychophysiological measures, self-reported ONP perceptions and use intentions, and ONP trial (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06192316). METHODS: Between 2024 and 2027, we will recruit 450 participants, comprised of: 150 young adults ages 18-24 who are susceptible but do not use tobacco; 150 young adults ages 18-24 who use tobacco; and 150 adults ages 25-65 who use tobacco. Participants complete procedures at an in-person laboratory visit. During the visit, participants complete pre-exposure self-report measures and are randomized between subjects to one of nine conditions in a 3 (Nicotine Concentration: None, Low, or High) x 3 (Nicotine Source Claim: None, Tobacco Free, or Synthetic) design. Within conditions, participants view 16 ONP pack images, in random order, reflecting different ONP brands and flavors. During exposure, we collect psychophysiological measures including heart rate, skin conductance, and visual attention. After exposure, participants complete self-report measures of ONP perceptions and use intentions, and a timed behavioral task where they are presented with ONP packages corresponding to their randomized condition and brands and flavors shown in the stimuli. Participants can try one of the products, and ONP trial is the behavioral outcome of interest. However, the packages do not contain ONPs; they contain commercially available pouches with food grade ingredients. At visit conclusion, participants are de-briefed and receive their incentive for participating. CONCLUSIONS: This project will generate evidence on the effects of nicotine concentration and source claims on ONP packaging in young adults who are not using but susceptible to tobacco, young adults using tobacco, and adults using tobacco to inform potential regulations.

item.title: Tumor Longevity: a time-dependent biomarker of immune checkpoint inhibitor responsiveness across head and neck, lung, renal and urothelial cancers.
item.dc:creator: Romanò R, Airoldi C, Alfieri S, Piemontese A, Pierri S, Calvanese G, Piscazzi D, Ciarlo G, Signorelli D, Pizzutilo EG, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Romanò R, Airoldi C, Alfieri S, Piemontese A, Pierri S, Calvanese G, Piscazzi D, Ciarlo G, Signorelli D, Pizzutilo EG, et al.
Journal: The oncologist | DOI: 10.1093/oncolo/oyag445
Published: 2026-Nov-06
PMID: 42992952



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: the duration of tumor persistence within the host-defined as Tumor Longevity (TL) - may capture cumulative biological and immunologic interactions, shaping immunotherapy treatment response. However, the impact of TL on outcomes with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) remains unexplored. We hypothesized that TL may reflect integrated tumor-host dynamics influencing ICI efficacy and investigated this association in patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), renal and urothelial cancer (R/UC). MATERIALS AND METHODS: we conducted a retrospective, observational study including adult patients with advanced HNSCC, NSCLC, R/UC receiving ICI (≥first line) across 2 Italian cancer centers. TL, defined as the time from first histological diagnosis to ICI initiation, was analyzed as a continuous variable using 3-knot restricted cubic spline models. Multivariable logistic and Cox regression analyses assessed associations between TL and disease control rate (DCR), grade (G)≥3 immune-related adverse events (irAEs), and overall survival (OS). RESULTS: 304 patients, diagnosed from 2002 to 2022, started ICI from 2014 to 2022. Median TL was 15.30 months (IQR 5.52-33.05). Overall DCR was 56.25% [95% CI 50.47; 61.91]; CTCAE G ≥ 3 irAEs occurred in 16 (5.2%) patients; 231 (76.0%) patients died. In multivariable analyses, longer TL was associated with higher DCR (OR Q3 vs. Q1 = 3.26; 95%CI 1.24; 8.59, p = 0.004), while no significant associations for G ≥ 3 irAEs (OR = 1.27; 95% CI 0.39-4.12) and OS (HR = 0.79; 95% CI 0.49-1.28; p = 0.407) were observed. CONCLUSIONS: These real-world, hypothesis-raising results suggest that TL may capture clinically relevant information associated with ICI outcomes. TL may represent a pragmatic, time-dependent biomarker integrating tumor behavior and host factors. Prospective and translational studies incorporating TL with molecular and immune profiling are warranted to elucidate whether this association reflects tumor biology, host factors, treatment history, or their combination.

Journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1002/ohn.70513
Published: 2026-Nov-06
PMID: 42992588



Abstract:
The Lenire system uses bimodal auditory and tongue stimulation to treat tinnitus. FDA-approved since 2023, the device has shown efficacy and safety in initial trials. Using the MAUDE database, we conducted preliminary post-market surveillance. This retrospective review analyzed reports of the Lenire device from 2023 to 2025. Event characteristics were examined for initial trends. The MAUDE database has limitations, including underreporting and reporting bias. Nine unique reports related to the Lenire device were extracted from MAUDE. The most commonly reported events included tinnitus exacerbation (n = 6), no tinnitus improvement (n = 2), and fatigue (n = 1). There was a single death from suicide temporally associated with device use and preceded by episodic tinnitus worsening, then overall improvement, but causality could not be established. Five patients had sustained tinnitus exacerbation after device discontinuation and were reportedly unaware of the potential treatment-related adverse effect. The findings, although limited by reporting bias and lack of validation, have identified reports of users who may experience adverse effects, including tinnitus exacerbation that may continue even after device discontinuation.

item.title: Endoscope-Assisted Transoral Resection for Pharyngeal and Laryngeal Vascular Malformations: A Surgical Technique.

Published: 2026-Nov-06

Abstract:
Pharyngolaryngeal vascular malformations (PLVMs) are commonly treated with sclerotherapy; however, its efficacy for localized protruding lesions is often limited and may require multiple sessions with a risk of airway edema. We describe an endoscope-assisted transoral technique using flexible-tip endoscopy and tailored laryngoscopic exposure for safe, function-preserving resection. This technique was applied in 7 patients with PLVMs. Surgical exposure was achieved using an FK-WO retractor or curved laryngoscope, and visualization was provided by a flexible-tip rigid endoscope. Resection was performed along the submucosal plane while avoiding intralesional incision. All procedures were completed successfully with minimal blood loss and no postoperative complications. Oral intake was resumed within 3 postoperative days, and no recurrence was observed during follow-up. Endoscope-assisted transoral resection provides a safe and effective treatment for selected PLVMs. This approach allows precise lesion control while preserving function and may represent an alternative to repeated sclerotherapy in appropriately selected patients.

item.title: Local and systemic inflammatory and immune pathways in anaplastic thyroid carcinoma: emerging therapeutic targets.
item.dc:creator: Ceruti D, van Houten P, Changoer P, Netea MG, Jaeger M, Netea-Maier RT
item.description:
Authors: Ceruti D, van Houten P, Changoer P, Netea MG, Jaeger M, Netea-Maier RT
Journal: Cancer treatment reviews | DOI: 10.1016/j.ctrv.2026.103240
Published: 2026-Nov-05
PMID: 43019925



Abstract:
Anaplastic thyroid cancer (ATC) is a rare endocrine cancer and one of the most lethal malignancies with only few treatment options. Most patients present with advanced and unresectable disease, and the median survival is approximately three months. In recent years, systemic treatments have become available for a subgroup of patients with ATC harboring targetable variants, such as BRAF/MEK inhibitors for patients with pathogenetic BRAFV600E variants. However, only a small proportion of patients with ATC are eligible for these treatments, and most treated patients develop resistant and progressive disease. Hence, an urgent need remains for new treatment approaches. Accumulating evidence underlines the roles of systemic inflammation, immunosuppressive and protumoral immune cells tumor infiltration, and elevated numbers of circulating proinflammatory myeloid immune cells in tumor angiogenesis, metastasis, and disease progression of ATC. In this review, we highlight recent advances in understanding the pathogenesis of ATC and summarize latest trends in systemic treatments for patients with ATC. Moreover, based on these developments in understanding the pathophysiology of the disease, we propose how targeting different protumoral processes could lead to future treatment modalities for patients with ATC, with a specific focus on inflammatory processes and the innate immune system.

item.title: A Global Perspective on Calibration and Standardization in Oral Cancer Screening Training.
item.dc:creator: Zain RB, Ramanathan A, Ghani WMN
item.description:
Authors: Zain RB, Ramanathan A, Ghani WMN
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70559
Published: 2026-Nov-05
PMID: 42989832



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early oral cancer detection improves survival, but diagnosing early, asymptomatic lesions remains challenging. Screening effectiveness depends heavily on examiner competency, highlighting the need for structured training and calibration. OBJECTIVE: This narrative review examines the evolution, current practices, and future directions of examiner training, calibration, and standardization in global oral cancer screening. REVIEW FINDINGS: Existing training programs vary widely in content, duration, and assessment. While structured approaches combining theoretical instruction, image-based learning, and supervised clinical training enhance diagnostic accuracy, published studies provide limited details on training protocols, calibration procedures, and competency benchmarks. Formal assessment of inter-examiner reliability, periodic recalibration, and standardized quality assurance are inconsistently reported. Models like OralDETECT demonstrate scalable, competency-based frameworks. Additionally, empowering community health workers through artificial intelligence, mobile health, and adjunctive diagnostic tools provides promising opportunities to expand screening capacity in resource-limited settings. CONCLUSION: Establishing an internationally standardized framework for examiner training, competency assessment, and continuous quality assurance is essential to improve screening reliability and reduce global oral cancer mortality. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Structured training and calibration bridge critical diagnostic gaps among primary healthcare practitioners. Integrating these standardized protocols with digital health innovations enhances triage accuracy, overcomes geographic barriers, and optimizes risk-based screening models.

item.title: Systemic Therapies for Recurrent Aphthous Stomatitis: A Systematic Review of Efficacy and Safety.
item.dc:creator: Sánchez Sáez G, Gómez García FJ, Ruíz Roca JA, Galera Molero F
item.description:
Authors: Sánchez Sáez G, Gómez García FJ, Ruíz Roca JA, Galera Molero F
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70560
Published: 2026-Nov-05
PMID: 42989707



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of systemic pharmacological and nutritional interventions for recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS). MATERIALS AND METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020, five databases were searched for studies published from 2001 to 2026. Clinical trials and analytical observational studies of systemic treatments for RAS were included. Risk of bias was assessed using design-appropriate tools. Owing to clinical and methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized qualitatively. RESULTS: Twenty studies were included: 16 randomized trials, three non-randomized intervention studies, and one observational cohort. Interventions included corticosteroids, colchicine, thalidomide, levamisole, pentoxifylline, dapsone, clofazimine, sulodexide, montelukast, roflumilast, rebamipide, vitamin B12, vitamin C, multivitamins, zinc, and omega-3 fatty acids. Several therapies improved pain, ulcer burden, healing, or recurrence-related outcomes, but comparative evidence was inconsistent. Thalidomide showed potential benefit but important safety limitations and a high risk of bias. Nutritional interventions showed mixed results. CONCLUSIONS: Selected systemic therapies may benefit severe, frequent, or refractory RAS, but no intervention can be considered clearly superior. Evidence certainty is limited by heterogeneity, small samples, limited direct comparisons, and risk of bias.

item.title: Direct Oral Healthcare Costs Associated With Xerostomia and Hyposalivation: A Scoping Review and Annual Cost Synthesis.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To map the available evidence on direct oral healthcare costs associated with xerostomia and hyposalivation. METHODS: A scoping review was conducted following PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Searches were performed in PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science, with additional screening of gray literature. Studies reporting direct oral healthcare costs associated with xerostomia or/and hyposalivation were eligible. Reported costs were standardized to a common currency and price year. CONCLUSION: The evidence base is limited and heterogeneous. The exploratory annual synthesis provides an initial framework for mapping reported cost components but does not represent a definitive estimate of economic burden.

item.title: Metronomic Tegafur-Uracil Maintenance Therapy in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma Following Adjuvant Chemoradiotherapy.
item.dc:creator: Lu HJ, Chiu YW, Tseng HC, Peng CY, Hsin CH, Chuang CY, Wu MF, Huang WS

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCSCC) is the predominant subtype of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma in Taiwan. Despite the guideline-recommended adjuvant chemoradiotherapy (CRT) for advanced pathological risk factors, long-term survival remains suboptimal. We evaluated the efficacy of tegafur-uracil as metronomic maintenance therapy following adjuvant CRT. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study analyzed 197 OCSCC patients who underwent curative resection followed by adjuvant CRT. Patients were stratified by receipt of metronomic tegafur-uracil maintenance therapy. Survival outcomes were assessed using Cox proportional hazards regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses. RESULTS: Patients receiving metronomic maintenance therapy (49.2%, 97/197) demonstrated favorable survival trends compared with those who did not. Five-year disease-free survival and disease-specific survival rates were 57.4% vs. 53.0% (p = 0.101), and 70.1% versus 60.8% (p = 0.092), respectively. Patients with ≥ 2 risk factors-extreme body mass index, positive margins, extranodal extension, and advanced depth of invasion-demonstrated significantly better outcomes following metronomic maintenance therapy. Therapy initiation at 1-3 months post-CRT and a treatment duration exceeding 12 months were also associated with a better prognosis. CONCLUSION: Metronomic tegafur-uracil maintenance therapy was associated with favorable outcomes, particularly in patients presenting with ≥ 2 identified risk factors. Prospective multicenter validation is warranted.

item.dc:creator: El Shatanofy M, Sargi Z, Nisenbaum E
item.description:
Authors: El Shatanofy M, Sargi Z, Nisenbaum E
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70538
Published: 2026-Nov-05
PMID: 42989572



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Skull base reconstruction has continued to evolve in parallel with advances in endoscopic skull base ablation in order to accomplish the goal of restoring larger and more complicated defects between the cranial and nasal cavities while balancing morbidity, cost, and recovery. METHODS: We reviewed recent literature on advances in skull base reconstruction including graded endoscopic reconstruction, appropriate use of perioperative adjuncts, endoscopic free tissue inset, patient-specific planning, dural substitutes, regenerative scaffolds, and autologous biologics. RESULTS: Graded reconstruction supports free grafts or local flaps for selected low-flow defects and multilayer vascularized closure for high-flow defects. Lumbar drainage benefits selected high-risk patients, whereas routine packing and prolonged antibiotic prophylaxis are not consistently supported. Endoscopic free flap inset, virtual surgical planning, and patient-specific implants expand options for complex composite and salvage defects. Synthetic dural substitutes can reduce donor-site morbidity in appropriate cases. Leukocyte- and platelet-rich fibrin (L-PRF) has emerging clinical support, while most regenerative scaffolds, platelet-rich plasma (PRP), and cell-based strategies remain preclinical. CONCLUSIONS: With advancements in skull base reconstruction, the paradigm has shifted toward using the least morbid construct that reliably restores the intracranial-sinonasal barrier while preserving function and quality of life. Standardized, prospective studies with attention to patient- and value-centric outcomes are crucial for improving care. Material science advances will continue to expand reconstructive options.

item.title: Perioperative Antibiotic Use in Head and Neck Surgery.
item.dc:creator: Blaurock M, Szturz P, Mueller SA, Knoke M, Höpfner N, Hübner NO, Inhestern J, Colombo E, Busch CJ, Maniakas A
item.description:
Authors: Blaurock M, Szturz P, Mueller SA, Knoke M, Höpfner N, Hübner NO, Inhestern J, Colombo E, Busch CJ, Maniakas A
Journal: JAMA network open | DOI: 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.42922
Published: 2026-Nov-02
PMID: 43002397



Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis in head and neck surgery remains poorly standardized internationally, despite evidence supporting short-course regimens and showing no benefit in low-risk procedures. Contemporary international data on prescribing practice are limited. OBJECTIVES: To characterize international patterns of perioperative antibiotic use in endocrine and oncologic head and neck surgery and to identify discrepancies between reported practice and evidence-based recommendations. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: In this survey study, a cross-sectional survey was distributed electronically between October 1, 2024, and December 31, 2025, through national and international professional societies. Respondents were classified by country of practice into Europe, North America, and rest of world. Data were analyzed in June 2026. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Routine antibiotic use, agent selection, and duration of prophylaxis across 6 procedure categories (conventional thyroidectomy, completion thyroidectomy, complex thyroidectomy, low-risk head and neck squamous cell carcinoma [HNSCC], low-complexity HNSCC, and complex clean-contaminated HNSCC). Secondary outcomes were departmental guideline availability and circumstances prompting antibiotic use. RESULTS: Of 468 respondents (310 of 419 [74%] with available data reported male sex or gender, 32 of 432 [82%] otolaryngologists-head and neck surgeons and 283 of 431 [66%] in academic practice), routine antibiotic use for conventional thyroidectomy was reported by 12% (95% CI, 8%-19%) of European, 35% (95% CI, 27%-44%) of North American, and 56% (95% CI, 39%-71%) of rest of world respondents. For clean-contaminated HNSCC, prophylaxis use ranged from 93% to 99%, with aminopenicillin plus a β-lactamase inhibitor preferred in Europe (66%) and North America (64%); cefazolin predominated in North America (47%) and cefuroxime in Europe (31%). For low-complexity clean-contaminated procedures, 24-hour regimens were reported by 43% (95% CI, 34%-53%) of North American vs 11% (95% CI, 7%-16%) of European respondents, whereas 7-day courses were reported by 23% (95% CI, 17%-29%) of European vs 8% (95% CI, 4%-15%) of North American respondents. Departmental HNSCC guidelines were more available in Europe than North America (83% vs 38%). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this survey study of 468 head and neck surgeons, perioperative antibiotic prescribing was heterogeneous internationally, with routine use in clean procedures and prolonged regimens for clean-contaminated surgery. Departmental guideline availability did not correspond to shorter reported prophylaxis duration, suggesting that implementation rather than guideline existence may be the target for antimicrobial stewardship.

item.title: Extent of lymphadenectomy dictates adjuvant chemotherapy benefit in primarily resected esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: a multi-cohort validation.
item.dc:creator: Huang Y, Lin X, Lin Y, Han Z
item.description:
Authors: Huang Y, Lin X, Lin Y, Han Z
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1920549
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43022032



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: While primary surgery remains a crucial treatment for resectable esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), the uniform application of postoperative adjuvant chemotherapy for pathologically node-positive patients exposes many to severe systemic toxicity. This study hypothesizes the existence of a specific lymph node dissection (LND) threshold that stratifies the survival benefit of adjuvant chemotherapy and aims to define this cutpoint to enable safe therapeutic de-escalation. METHODS: We conducted a multi-cohort retrospective study using data from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database (n = 753, training cohort) and a Chinese single-center repository (n = 447, validation cohort) of patients with ESCC who underwent primary radical esophagectomy without radiotherapy. The optimal prognostic cutpoint for LND was mathematically determined using X-tile software. An interactive Cox proportional hazards nomogram incorporating an LND-by-chemotherapy interaction term was developed and validated. Subsequently, layer-specific 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) was performed within separate surgical strata of the validation cohort to assess chemotherapy efficacy. RESULTS: X-tile analysis established 21 lymph nodes as the optimal LND threshold. Multivariable analysis confirmed that adequate LND (≥ 21 nodes) and adjuvant chemotherapy were independent protective prognostic factors. The interactive nomogram demonstrated good discrimination and calibration across both populations. Crucially, layer-specific PSM in the external validation cohort revealed divergent therapeutic responses dependent on surgical quality. For patients with suboptimal LND (< 21 nodes), adjuvant chemotherapy provided a significant survival benefit over surgery alone (P = 0.048). In contrast, for patients achieving an adequate LND (≥21 nodes), the addition of adjuvant chemotherapy yielded no further survival advantage (P = 0.085). CONCLUSIONS: Achieving the removal of ≥ 21 lymph nodes serves as a robust anatomical biomarker that fundamentally alters the postoperative therapeutic landscape for ESCC. Patients with suboptimal LND require adjuvant chemotherapy to compensate for potential residual disease, whereas those achieving the 21-node clearance threshold derive no additional survival benefit from systemic interventions and can be safely exempted from cytotoxic over-treatment.

item.title: Malignant transformation of an intracranial epidermoid cyst into squamous cell carcinoma: a case report and systematic review.
item.dc:creator: Onzere LE, Ma J, Stephano EE, Kisangai PM, Li Y, Quan W, Wu Y
item.description:
Authors: Onzere LE, Ma J, Stephano EE, Kisangai PM, Li Y, Quan W, Wu Y
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1978480
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43016707



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Intracranial epidermoid cysts (IECs) are rare, benign congenital lesions that occasionally undergo malignant transformation into squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). This study presents a rare case of an IEC in the anterior cranial fossa transforming into SCC and reviews existing literature to summarize clinical characteristics, treatment strategies, and survival outcomes. METHODS: We detail the clinical presentation, management and long-term follow-up of a 52-year-old female who developed SCC 75 months after initial subtotal resection of an anterior cranial fossa IEC. We also conducted a comprehensive systematic literature search across PubMed, MEDLINE and CNKI in accordance with PRISMA guidelines compiling 59 well-documented cases (including our index case) to analyze demographic features, transformation intervals, treatment modalities and overall survival. RESULTS: Our patient underwent repeat subtotal tumor resection followed by adjuvant intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT). She maintained a disease-free survival (DFS) of 14 months post-radiotherapy (17 months post-reoperation) until July 2026, when she developed multifocal intraventricular recurrence. The literature review revealed a mean patient age of 54.7 years with an equal gender distribution (1.03:1). The cerebellopontine angle (CPA) was the most frequent tumor site (50.85%). The mean interval from IEC diagnosis to malignant transformation was 9.24 years. Prognosis for transformed SCC remains poor, with a median overall survival of 6 months. However, patients treated with surgery combined with radiotherapy demonstrated significantly improved outcomes (median survival 13 months) compared to those undergoing surgery alone (41 days). CONCLUSIONS: Malignant transformation of IECs into SCC is a rare, aggressive complication. Long-term surveillance with contrast-enhanced MRI is vital for patients with previously resected IECs. Early detection, maximal safe surgical resection followed by adjuvant radiotherapy currently offers the most favorable survival benefit.

item.title: Development and validation of a magnetic resonance imaging-based model for the prediction of progression-free survival before initial treatment of hypopharyngeal cancer treated with chemoradiation.
item.dc:creator: Tao H, Wei J, Zheng Q, Yang X, Sun Y
item.description:
Authors: Tao H, Wei J, Zheng Q, Yang X, Sun Y
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1928542
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43016519



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop a radiomics-clinical model for prediction of the progression-free survival (PFS) in hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (HPSCC) patients treated with concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT). MATERIALS AND METHODS: One hundred and thirteen patients with hypopharyngeal cancers treated by CCRT were enrolled and randomly divided into training (N = 80) and validation (N = 33) groups. Python's PyRadiomics toolkit was used to extract radiomic features from magnetic resonance diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) sequences, which included four categories: shape (14), first-order (230), texture (306), and wavelet (738). All feature preprocessing steps-including normalization, intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) filtering, Pearson correlation filtering, and feature selection-were performed exclusively within the training set, with the same preprocessing parameters subsequently applied to the validation set. The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) penalized Cox regression algorithm with ten-fold cross-validation was used to screen key radiomic features and construct the Rad-score. We used Kaplan-Meier analysis and log-rank tests to assess the ability of the radiomic signature to stratify PFS risk, and constructed a radiomics nomogram to predict individual PFS probabilities at 1 and 2 years. RESULTS: The radiomics model consisting of six important features performed well in classifying patients into high- and low-risk groups of progression in both the training and test groups (log-rank test, p = 0.006 in the training cohort; p = 0.023 in the validation cohort, using the cutoff value of 0.025 determined from the training set). Age and T stage were chosen as clinically important variables based on univariate Cox regression analysis (p < 0.05). The radiomics nomogram demonstrated good differentiation ability, with C-indices of 0.904 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.816-0.992) and 0.858 (95% CI, 0.690-1.000) in the training and validation cohorts, respectively. The time-dependent AUCs for predicting 1-year and 2-year PFS were 0.867 and 0.837, respectively, in the training cohort, and 0.737 and 0.715 in the validation cohort. CONCLUSION: The multiparametric DWI-based radiomics model may serve as a potential tool to predict PFS in patients with HPSCC treated with CCRT after further prospective validation.

item.title: A study on the temporal network characteristics of early post-chemotherapy core symptoms in colorectal cancer patients based on ecological momentary assessment.
item.dc:creator: Lv Y, Xu L, Li M, Cai X, Ye L, Wang X, Wang X, Chen Y, Lu Y
item.description:
Authors: Lv Y, Xu L, Li M, Cai X, Ye L, Wang X, Wang X, Chen Y, Lu Y
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1942076
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43010921



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) often experience multiple concurrent symptoms during the early post-chemotherapy period, and both symptom severity and inter-symptom associations may change over time. Previous low-frequency assessments may not adequately capture short-term fluctuations. OBJECTIVE: To characterize the dynamic trajectories and network features of early symptoms in patients receiving postoperative adjuvant chemotherapy for CRC and to identify candidate symptoms for enhanced monitoring. METHODS: A prospective longitudinal study was conducted. Ecological momentary assessment (EMA) was performed three times daily for seven consecutive days after infusion in the first and second chemotherapy cycles and covered 13 symptoms. Linear mixed-effects models characterized symptom trajectories, and a multilevel vector autoregressive (mlVAR) model estimated temporal and contemporaneous networks. Edge uncertainty, centrality stability, sensitivity analyses, and between-cycle differences were evaluated. RESULTS: A total of 110 patients contributed 4,134 valid assessments (completion rate, 89.5%). All 13 symptoms showed significant time effects. Fatigue, loss of appetite, gastrointestinal symptoms, and sleep disturbance fluctuated, whereas numbness/tingling and depression showed cumulative trends. Loss of appetite, dry mouth, and nausea had comparatively high outgoing temporal associations. The strongest individual temporal edge was modest (standardized coefficient approximately 0.12). No statistically significant between-cycle differences were found in overall network structure or global strength. CONCLUSION: Early post-chemotherapy symptoms showed dynamic changes and a broadly comparable network structure across the first two cycles. Loss of appetite, dry mouth, and nausea may be candidates for enhanced monitoring and future intervention research; the observational findings do not establish causal effects or intervention efficacy.

item.title: Global burden, geographic and sex disparities, and projections to 2050 for salivary gland cancer across G20 countries: a GLOBOCAN 2024 analysis.
item.dc:creator: Yang W, Ma Y, Shu C
item.description:
Authors: Yang W, Ma Y, Shu C
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1995714
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43005071



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Salivary gland cancer is uncommon, and neither its distribution nor its trajectory across the G20 has been well described. Using the GLOBOCAN 2024 case counts, we described the 2024 burden in the 19 G20 member economies and in four HDI aggregates, and examined HDI-related gradients in population-level proxies for survival. METHODS: We analyzed the GLOBOCAN 2024 case counts for salivary-gland cancer (ICD-10 C07-C08) in the 19 G20 member economies and four HDI groups. Age-standardized incidence (ASIR) and mortality (ASMR) rates, 5-year prevalence, and the mortality-to-incidence (MIR) and prevalence-to-mortality (PMR) ratios were tabulated by country, HDI group and sex, and related to HDI using Spearman rank correlation. Projections to 2050 follow the GLOBOCAN 2024 Cancer Tomorrow default demographic scenario, applying the 2024 case counts and age-specific rates to United Nations population projections. RESULTS: In 2024 the G20 recorded 37,812 cases and 12,661 deaths, 46.2% of them in China and India. At country level, the HDI-MIR correlation was not significant (r = -0.04, 95% CI -0.48 to 0.42; P = 0.88), although MIR was highest in the low-HDI group (0.53) and lowest in the very-high-HDI group (0.34) and PMR varied 3.9-fold across aggregates. Male MIR exceeded female MIR in 16 of the 17 economies for which the ratio was computable, the sole exception being Türkiye. Holding 2024 age-specific rates constant, deaths at ages ≥75 years would rise by 152.8% by 2050; growth would be largest in the low- and medium-HDI aggregates (+134.4% and +96.1%) and smallest in Japan (+8.4%). CONCLUSION: The G20 burden was highly heterogeneous. Across the global HDI aggregates the burden followed development level, with the highest MIR in the low-HDI group, but this ordering did not carry over to a country-level HDI-MIR correlation among the 19 member economies. Projected growth was concentrated in low- and medium-HDI settings, which argues for strengthening diagnostic capacity and survivorship measurement there.

item.title: Association between absolute lymphocyte count and outcomes of radiotherapy combined with immunotherapy in elderly patients with inoperable esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Jiang Y, Chen W, Ni D, Liang X
item.description:
Authors: Jiang Y, Chen W, Ni D, Liang X
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1953153
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42997324



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether pretreatment absolute lymphocyte count (ALC) is related to clinical outcomes among elderly patients with inoperable ESCC receiving definitive radiotherapy combined with immunotherapy. METHODS: Elderly patients (≥ 60 years) with incurable ESCC who underwent programmed death-1 (PD-1) inhibitor therapy and definitive radiotherapy were retrospectively enrolled. ROC analysis identified the most discriminative ALC cutoff. Short-term efficacy was compared between groups, and Cox regression assessed factors related to overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). RESULTS: Data from 102 elderly patients were evaluated. The objective response rate (ORR) was 70.59%; median PFS and OS were 21 and 28 months, respectively. ROC analysis identified 1.24 × 109/L as the cutoff value for ALC. The response rate was markedly higher among patients with high ALC than among those with low ALC (86.0% vs. 51.1%, P < 0.001). ALC was identified as an independent factor associated with short-term treatment response by multivariate logistic regression (OR = 4.716, 95% CI: 1.167-19.062, P = 0.030). Longer median OS and PFS were observed in high-ALC patients. In the multivariate Cox analysis, higher ALC remained independently related to improved PFS (HR = 0.450, 95% CI 0.213-0.951, P = 0.036) and improved OS (HR = 0.425, 95% CI 0.184-0.982, P = 0.045). CONCLUSION: Baseline ALC has the potential to be used to guide patient selection and individualized treatment planning, because this readily available biomarker was independently associated with treatment response and survival.

item.title: Prognostic significance of lymph node staging in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy.
item.dc:creator: Han H, Hou X, Liu Y, Cai W, Jin J, Qiu X, Zhu Z, Zhao K, Hu M, Xue Z
item.description:
Authors: Han H, Hou X, Liu Y, Cai W, Jin J, Qiu X, Zhu Z, Zhao K, Hu M, Xue Z
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1931817
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42996502



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (nCIT) has emerged as a standard treatment for locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). This study aimed to evaluate the independent prognostic value of postoperative pathological N stage (ypN) and to assess whether pre-treatment clinical N stage (cN) provides additional prognostic information in patients achieving ypN0. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 194 ESCC patients who received nCIT followed by radical esophagectomy between January 2019 and December 2024. Patients were stratified into three groups: cN0/ypN0 (n=104), cN+/ypN0 (n=32), and ypN+ (n=58). Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models were used for survival analysis. Multivariable models were constructed using a clinically informed variable-selection strategy constrained by the number of events. For the three pairwise comparisons, unadjusted P values were compared against a Bonferroni-adjusted significance threshold of alpha=0.017 (0.05/3). RESULTS: A total of 194 patients were enrolled, with 31 deaths and 37 recurrences during a median follow-up of 34.0 months (reverse Kaplan-Meier). ypN+ patients had significantly worse overall survival (OS) and recurrence-free survival (RFS) than ypN- patients (both Log-rank P<0.001). In the primary multivariable model, ypN+ was an independent adverse prognostic factor for OS (HR = 3.204, 95%CI: 1.563-6.568, P = 0.001) and RFS (HR = 3.780, 95%CI: 1.943-7.356, P<0.001), and remained robust across extended, cycle-adjusted, and landmark sensitivity analyses. Among the three groups, ypN+ showed significantly shorter OS compared with both ypN0 groups (P = 0.002 vs cN0/ypN0; P = 0.008 vs cN+/ypN0; both below the Bonferroni threshold) and shorter RFS compared with cN0/ypN0 (P<0.001). No significant difference was observed between cN0/ypN0 and cN+/ypN0 groups for OS (P = 0.259); the RFS comparison was nominally significant but did not survive Bonferroni correction (HR = 2.799, 95%CI: 1.048-7.479, unadjusted P = 0.040). CONCLUSION: Postoperative ypN stage is the core prognostic determinant in ESCC after nCIT. In patients achieving ypN0, pre-treatment cN did not demonstrate statistically significant additional prognostic discrimination in this cohort, although estimates were imprecise due to the small cN+/ypN0 subgroup and limited events. Postoperative risk assessment should be based primarily on ypN status; these findings require validation in larger, preferably multicenter, cohorts.

item.title: Application of chimeric flaps for complex orbitomaxillary reconstruction in sinonasal malignancy.
item.dc:creator: Panchal K, Manikantan K, Samadder S, Arun P, Kekatpure VD, Jain PV, Sahu G
item.description:
Authors: Panchal K, Manikantan K, Samadder S, Arun P, Kekatpure VD, Jain PV, Sahu G
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1963043
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42996499



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sinonasal malignancies are rare tumors, and a subset of these patients presents with involvement of the orbitomaxillary area, resulting in a complex maxillectomy defect, which warrants primary reconstruction. Complexity increases with globe preservation, which mandates structural support to the globe, ideally reconstructed using a vascularized osseous flap. Such complex defect reconstruction requires multiple components, which are titrated according to the complex three-dimensional defects. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate the outcomes of primary orbitomaxillary reconstruction in sinonasal malignancy using multicomponent chimeric flaps, which included osseous chimeric flaps for globe-preserving total maxillectomy and soft tissue chimeric flaps for the remaining orbitomaxillary defects. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective observational study was conducted between June 2024 and April 2026 at a tertiary referral center. The cohort included consecutive patients with modified Brown type 3 to 6 maxillectomy defects having sinonasal malignancy, which were primarily reconstructed with chimeric flaps. Data on the pathology, type of orbito maxillectomy defects, and types and components of chimeric flaps were collected. Outcomes were measured by flap survival, re-explorations, wound healing compromise, and delays in the start of adjuvant therapy. Specifically for orbital preservation patients, further assessment was made on the presence of diplopia or enophthalmos. RESULTS: All 11 patients included in the study underwent a chimeric flap for orbitomaxillary defects. The most common pathology was squamous cell carcinoma. Seven (64%) were soft tissue chimeric flaps, and four (36%) were osseous chimeric flaps. All flaps survived completely. Satisfactory wound healing and contour restoration were achieved in all patients. CONCLUSION: Chimeric flaps with their multiple components, which can be contoured according to the complex three-dimensional orbitomaxillary defects, achieves primary healing. For total maxillectomy with globe preservation, bone reconstruction is warranted. Orbital bone reconstruction use of 3D model for contouring the bone strut and the orbital floor mesh can achieve accurate reconstruction for such complex defects.

item.title: Outcomes of sequential microvascular tissue transfer for radiation induced sequelae post mandibular reconstruction.
item.dc:creator: Panchal K, Ukil S, Kalwadia N, Samadder S, Manikantan K, Arun P, Kekatpure VD, Jain PV, Sahu GC
item.description:
Authors: Panchal K, Ukil S, Kalwadia N, Samadder S, Manikantan K, Arun P, Kekatpure VD, Jain PV, Sahu GC
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1897431
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42996241



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radiotherapy-related complications following mandibular reconstruction remain a major challenge in head and neck oncologic reconstruction. Although free fibula flap reconstruction has become the gold standard for segmental mandibular defects, delayed radiation-induced sequelae such as hardware exposure, contour deformity, soft tissue atrophy, fistula formation continue to affect long-term outcomes. Literature regarding the role of sequential microvascular tissue transfer in managing these complications remains limited. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate the indications, surgical planning, recipient vessel selection, and outcomes of sequential microvascular free tissue transfer performed for radiation-induced sequelae after mandibular reconstruction. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective observational study was conducted between June 2024 and December 2025 at a tertiary referral center. Patients who had previously undergone primary mandibular reconstruction using a fibula free flap followed by adjuvant radiotherapy and later developed radiation-related complications requiring secondary microvascular reconstruction were included. Demographic data, primary reconstructive details, radiation parameters, duration between radiation and complication, indications for sequential reconstruction, flap characteristics, recipient vessel selection, postoperative complications, and healing outcomes were analyzed. RESULTS: Ten patients were included in the study. All patients had undergone primary fibula free flap reconstruction following segmental mandibulectomy followed by sequential microvascular soft tissue reconstruction for radiation induced complications. Ipsilateral superficial temporal vessels were used as recipient vessels in all cases without using vein grafts. All flaps survived completely. Satisfactory wound healing and contour restoration were achieved in all patients. CONCLUSION: Sequential microvascular reconstruction represents a reliable and effective strategy for managing radiation-induced complications following mandibular reconstruction. Volume loss can be addressed during plate removal surgery which not only achieves a stable soft tissue cover but also prevents further progression to osteoradionecrosis.

item.title: The cervicovaginal microbiome as a candidate correlate and potential predictor of HPV clearance and treatment response after HSIL therapy: a scoping review.
item.dc:creator: Mwesige B, Angucia B, Mbodi L, Mwazha A, Niyonzima N, Mwansa-Kambafwile J, Breiman RF, Zakumumpa H, Chikandiwa A
item.description:
Authors: Mwesige B, Angucia B, Mbodi L, Mwazha A, Niyonzima N, Mwansa-Kambafwile J, Breiman RF, Zakumumpa H, Chikandiwa A
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1972845
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42991095



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) infection causes virtually all high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL) and cervical cancer, but only a minority progress, implicating host and microenvironmental cofactors. The cervicovaginal microbiome (CVM), particularly Lactobacillus-dominated communities, may influence hrHPV persistence, clearance, and response to HSIL treatment. OBJECTIVE: To map evidence linking the CVM with hrHPV clearance and outcomes after HSIL treatment, including loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP) and conization, using PRISMA-ScR and Arksey and O'Malley frameworks. METHODS: Literature on cervicovaginal microbiota, community state types (CSTs), HPV natural history, HSIL/CIN treatment, probiotics, microbiome-directed interventions, and predictive biomarkers was systematically searched and narratively synthesized using a Population-Concept-Context framework. RESULTS: Sixty-six sources were charted. Lactobacillus crispatus-dominated communities (CST-I) were associated with hrHPV clearance and favorable post-treatment outcomes, whereas CST-IV, bacterial vaginosis, and increased alpha-diversity were associated with hrHPV persistence, greater HSIL severity, and treatment failure. Proposed mechanisms include lactic acid-mediated pH regulation, D-lactic acid signaling, and modulation of viral oncoproteins and immune responses. Excision altered the CVM, with restoration of Lactobacillus dominance accompanying viral clearance. Microbial-signature machine-learning models showed promising but preliminary predictive performance. Oral and intravaginal probiotics showed inconsistent but generally favorable trends, with strongest evidence for intravaginal L. crispatus transplantation. Gut microbiome diversity may also influence chemoradiotherapy outcomes in invasive cervical cancer. CONCLUSION: The CVM is a promising predictor of hrHPV clearance and HSIL treatment response. However, methodological heterogeneity, small cohorts, and limited prospective evidence restrict clinical translation. Large prospective studies and rigorously designed trials are needed to validate predictive signatures and determine whether microbiome profiling or targeted modulation can improve HSIL management and outcomes.

item.title: PF chemotherapy combined with a PD-1/CTLA-4 bispecific antibody as first-line treatment in patients with recurrent/metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: a prospective, single-arm, phase II clinical study.

Abstract:
PURPOSE: This study evaluated the antitumor activity and safety of cadonilimab, a programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1)/cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated protein 4 (CTLA-4) bispecific antibody, combined with platinum/carboplatin and 5-fluorouracil (PF) chemotherapy as first-line treatment for patients with recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (R/M HNSCC). METHODS: In this prospective, single-arm, phase II trial, patients with histopathologically confirmed R/M HNSCC received cadonilimab (10 mg/kg) plus PF chemotherapy every 3 weeks for 4-6 cycles, followed by maintenance cadonilimab. The primary endpoint was 1-year progression-free survival (PFS). A target sample size of 30 was planned, but the study was terminated prematurely after enrolling 16 patients due to slow accrual. At a median follow-up of 18.4 months (range, 4.6 - 39.6), the 1-year PFS and overall survival (OS) rates were 50.0% (95% CI: 30.6% - 81.6%) and 75.0% (95% CI: 56.5% - 99.5%), respectively. The Objective Response Rate (ORR) was 56.3% (95% CI: 29.9% - 80.2%). Median PFS and OS were 9.8 months (95% CI: 2.8 - NR) and 17.7 months (95% CI: 12.3 - NR), respectively.
