CONCLUSION: In this exploratory study, first-line cadonilimab combined with PF chemotherapy exhibited potential antitumor activity and manageable safety profiles in patients with R/M HNSCC. Given the favorable baseline profile of the cohort and the single-arm design, these findings should be interpreted with caution. Larger randomized controlled trials are required to determine whether dual PD-1/CTLA-4 blockade offers an incremental benefit over standard anti-PD-1-based regimens.

item.title: AICAR induces S phase cell cycle arrest in ESCC by targeting the AMPK/mTORC1 and mTORC2/AKT pathway.
item.dc:creator: Zou M, Zhang T, He L, Li J, Lin Z, Jia C, Ma K, Wang L, Xu S, Cai B, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Zou M, Zhang T, He L, Li J, Lin Z, Jia C, Ma K, Wang L, Xu S, Cai B, et al.
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1975805
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42990857



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: 5-Aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide-1-β-4-ribofuranoside (AICAR), an AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) agonist, exhibits potent antitumor capacity across various malignancies. However, its efficacy and underlying mechanisms in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remain largely unexplored. METHODS: We treated HEEC, TE1, and TE13 cells with AICAR and assessed proliferation, cell cycle distribution, and expression of key signaling proteins, followed by SN38 cotreatment to evaluate apoptosis and chemosensitization. RESULTS: AICAR treatment suppressed proliferation in all three cell lines but induced a distinct S-phase arrest specifically in ESCC cells. Mechanistically, AICAR activated AMPK, which concurrently inhibited the mTORC1 pathway via TSC2 phosphorylation and activated the mTORC2/AKT pathway through FOXO3-mediated transcriptional upregulation of Rictor. A critical difference was observed between cell types: in HEEC cells, AICAR treatment upregulated the tumor suppressor PTEN, which prevented full AKT activation. In contrast, ESCC cells, with unaltered PTEN and dysfunctional p53, sustained AKT hyperactivation. This drove cells into S-phase, where they were subsequently arrested due to the parallel inhibition of mTORC1. Furthermore, synchronizing ESCC cells in the S-phase with AICAR, followed by its withdrawal and subsequent treatment with SN38, significantly enhanced apoptosis. CONCLUSION: Our findings reveal that AICAR induces S-phase arrest in ESCC cells by dually modulating the mTORC1 and mTORC2/AKT signaling pathways. This differential effect, stemmed from dysfunctional p53/PTEN axis in ESCC cells, distinguishes ESCC cells from normal epithelial cells. Together, these results suggest that AICAR synchronizes ESCC cells in the S phase, thereby sensitizing them to S-phase-specific agents like SN38 and representing a potential novel strategy for ESCC treatment.

item.title: Anterior cingulate input tunes striatal dynamics for context-dependent social preference in a mouse model of autism.
item.dc:creator: Zhou Y, Xiao H, Feng D, López-Huerta VG, Wang K, Xi K, Hartley ND, Arias-Garcia MA, Liu T, Wang W, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Zhou Y, Xiao H, Feng D, López-Huerta VG, Wang K, Xi K, Hartley ND, Arias-Garcia MA, Liu T, Wang W, et al.
Journal: Nature communications | DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-79022-6
Published: 2026-Oct-20
PMID: 43003851



Abstract:
Social preference in autism spectrum disorder varies across contexts, but the underlying neural mechanisms remain unclear. Here we show that Shank3 knockout (KO) mice, an autism mouse model, exhibit reduced preference for social over nonsocial stimuli while retaining a preference for females over males. Calcium imaging reveals context-dependent differences between KO and wild-type (WT) mice in the organization of neuronal population dynamics in the dorsomedial striatum (DMS), corresponding to their behavioural preferences. Functional imaging and molecular analyses reveal reduced functional connectivity between the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) and DMS and molecular alterations more pronounced in the striatal matrix. ACC inhibition eliminates genotype-dependent differences in DMS dynamics. Inhibiting the ACC-DMS pathway impairs social preference, whereas its activation in KO mice shifts DMS dynamics towards WT patterns and improves social preference. These findings identify a cortical pathway that shapes striatal population dynamics and context-dependent social preference in an autism mouse model.

item.title: Parental EV-A71 vaccine hesitancy amid shifting HFMD pathogens: a cross-sectional study in Guangzhou.
item.dc:creator: Su X, Gao Z, Zhong J, Bai C, Xie R, Luo L, Wu Q
item.description:
Authors: Su X, Gao Z, Zhong J, Bai C, Xie R, Luo L, Wu Q
Journal: BMC public health | DOI: 10.1186/s12889-026-29951-0
Published: 2026-Oct-19
PMID: 43021215



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Following enterovirus A71 (EV‑A71) vaccine introduction, the hand foot mouth disease (HFMD) pathogen spectrum has shifted away from EV‑A71, prompting parental doubts about the vaccine's continued relevance. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence and determinants of EV‑A71 vaccine hesitancy among parents in Guangzhou. METHODS: We surveyed parents of children ≤ 5 years at 10 community health centers in Guangzhou using stratified multi-stage sampling. Exploratory factor analysis identified latent variables, followed by structural equation modeling (SEM) to examine their direct and indirect effects on vaccine hesitancy. Logistic regression with cluster-robust standard errors was used to assess the effects of parental knowledge, attitude, and practice (KAP) and physician recommendation practices, specifically examining the cross-level interaction between physician recommendation enthusiasm and parental vaccine confidence. RESULTS: The prevalence of EV-A71 vaccine hesitancy among parents was 28.95%. Mothers (OR: 0.46[0.28, 0.76]) and parents with a college degree or associate degree (OR: 0.53[0.32, 0.86]) were less hesitant, whereas being a non‑healthcare worker (OR: 2.38[1.03, 5.55]) and having a child without a history of HFMD (OR: 3.45[1.31, 9.12]) were more hesitant. SEM indicated that vaccine confidence (β = -0.39), service trust (β = -0.17), and risk perception (β = -0.17) exerted negative direct effects on vaccine hesitancy. Knowledge had no direct effect, its total indirect effect via the three mediators was significant(β = -0.45). Furthermore, the interaction between parental confidence and physician recommendation was marginally significant(β = 2.10, P = 0.08). CONCLUSION: Knowledge reduces hesitancy mainly through confidence, trust, and risk perception, not directly. Communication and counseling addressing these attitudes may support informed parental decisions about voluntary, self-paid EV-A71 vaccination.

Abstract:
Malawi polyomavirus (MWPyV) has been detected in respiratory and gastrointestinal specimens, mostly in children; however there are limited data on its distribution and diversity. Here, we analyse n = 233 oropharyngeal swabs, collected from pediatric patients in São Paulo State, Brazil for MWPyV and potential co-infections using an integrated molecular, phylogenetic, and ultrastructural approach. The genome of genotype III shows evidence of putative recombination events with genomic regions related to genotypes II and III. One genotype I sequence forms a distinct phylogenetic branch, suggesting an unsampled or transitional lineage. Our findings provide evidence into the genomic diversity, viral recombination and potentially diverging lineages of MWPyV in pediatric patients.

item.title: High fiber diet mitigates exposure risk of nanoplastics in male mice.
item.dc:creator: Yu Z, Abulipizi G, Fang Y, Qu C, Ding L, Zong Z, Huang J, Chen Z, Zhou J, Li Z, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Yu Z, Abulipizi G, Fang Y, Qu C, Ding L, Zong Z, Huang J, Chen Z, Zhou J, Li Z, et al.
Journal: Nature communications | DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78675-7
Published: 2026-Oct-15
PMID: 43015315



Abstract:
Potential health risk associated with dietary intake of nanoplastics has emerged as a global health concern, yet approaches for reducing gastrointestinal nanoplastic exposure remain poorly explored. Here, we investigated whether increasing dietary fiber intake influences the gastrointestinal fate of nanoplastics in male mice utilizing a visible/near-infrared dual fluorescence labeling technique combined with non-invasive imaging. The estimated retention rates of nanoplastics-associated fluorescence are decreased by two and seven times in male mice fed with medium fiber diet and high fiber diet compared to those with standard fiber diet, 24 h after oral intake. High fiber diet is associated with attenuated nanoplastics-induced epithelial damage to intestinal tract and declined detectable NIR fluorescence in important organs such as liver during 28-d oral exposure to nanoplastics. In vitro simulations show that dietary fiber physically encapsulates and adheres nanoplastics to decrease their bioavailability. Understanding how dietary constituents influence the gastrointestinal fate of nanoplastics may provide a scientific basis for the future development of dietary strategies aimed at reducing nanoplastic exposure.

item.title: Bioinspired nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides for treating comorbid anxiety and depression in inflammatory bowel disease.
item.dc:creator: Zhang F, Chen L, Wang S, Chen X, Du K, Song F, Jiang L, Feng Y, Du S, Jiang T, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Zhang F, Chen L, Wang S, Chen X, Du K, Song F, Jiang L, Feng Y, Du S, Jiang T, et al.
Journal: Nature communications | DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78633-3
Published: 2026-Oct-14
PMID: 43009500



Abstract:
Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic condition frequently accompanied by psychological comorbidities, such as anxiety and depression. Although current treatments may alleviate some of these symptoms, the intricate pathogenesis of these comorbidities highlights an urgent need for therapeutic strategies with combined anti-inflammatory, barrier-reparative, and microbiota-modulating effects. Herein, we develop a series of nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides (NZEP) by integrating nanozymes with yeast-derived polysaccharides using an insect sclerotization-inspired strategy. Among them, NZEPTA-Ce, with the highest degree of nanozyme-exoskeletonization, is capable of disrupting the inflammatory vicious cycle by inhibiting MAPK and NF-κB-mediated inflammatory signaling pathways. Oral administration of NZEPTA-Ce in mice enables effective retention and accumulation in inflamed colonic regions, reverses the homeostasis imbalance of intestinal inflammation and promotes intestinal barrier repair. Furthermore, NZEPTA-Ce treatment reverses gut microbiota dysbiosis and optimizes the composition of microbial metabolites, thereby alleviating anxiety and depressive symptoms associated with IBD. This study provides a safe and promising therapeutic strategy for the management of IBD patients and their associated psychological comorbidities.

item.title: Fruit-eating adaptations in a Late Cretaceous oviraptorosaur (Theropoda).
item.dc:creator: Funston GF, Dudgeon TW, Simon DJ, Dufault DM, Boyd C, Fowler D, Currie PJ, Evans DC
item.description:
Authors: Funston GF, Dudgeon TW, Simon DJ, Dufault DM, Boyd C, Fowler D, Currie PJ, Evans DC
Journal: Nature communications | DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78343-w
Published: 2026-Oct-10
PMID: 43003810



Abstract:
The diversification of herbivorous dinosaurs and the rise of angiosperms in the Late Cretaceous are each well established, but the link between them is debated. Broad-scale diversity patterns in the two groups appear not to closely align, and there is no direct evidence of dinosaur adaptation to angiosperm-based diets. Here we describe Infernogallus jamesi gen. et. sp. nov., a diminutive caenagnathid oviraptorosaur, and show that these theropods were specialised herbivores that originated alongside the rise of fleshy angiosperm fruits. The nearly complete, articulated skull of Infernogallus jamesi-the first for the clade-reveals drastic changes to the adductor musculature organisation, unique in non-avian theropods but converged upon by extant frugivorous parrots. These modifications enabled extensive oral processing of soft food using anteroposterior movement of the mandible and occlusion of ridges and grooves on opposed elements. Altogether, this attests to a highly specialised herbivorous diet in caenagnathids, which likely consisted in large part of fleshy angiosperm fruits, which increased in size and diversity in concert with the radiation of oviraptorosaurs. Caenagnathids thus provide one of the strongest candidates for angiosperm-based diet adaptations in dinosaurs, but their role in the Late Cretaceous proliferation of fruit-which shaped early Cenozoic flora-remains unclear.

item.title: Multimodal Deep Learning Prognostic Model for Predicting Treatment Outcomes for Oropharyngeal Carcinoma.

Abstract:
PURPOSE: Accurate prediction of locoregional recurrence (LRR) in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) is needed to guide treatment de-escalation decisions, but validated prognostic models integrating imaging and clinical data are lacking. We developed and evaluated a multimodal deep learning model combining pretreatment computed tomography (CT) with clinical variables to predict LRR. METHODS: In this retrospective multicenter prognostic study, we assembled 1,384 patients with histologically confirmed OPSCC treated with definitive radiotherapy with or without concurrent chemotherapy and without surgical resection of the primary tumor. Data were drawn from 1 private institutional archive and five publicly available archives. A cross-attention model fusing CT and clinical features was compared with feature concatenation, clinical-only, and imaging-only models. The primary outcome was LRR. Discrimination was assessed by Harrell Concordance Index (C-index) across 3-fold cross-validation, and risk stratification by Kaplan-Meier analysis with log-rank testing. Attribution analysis was used to identify influential predictors. RESULTS: LRR occurred in 161 of 1,384 patients (11.6%) over a median follow-up of 59.8 months (interquartile range, 25.8-89.0 months). The cross-attention model achieved the highest mean C-index, 0.718 (range, 0.699-0.734), followed by the clinical-only (0.705; range, 0.680-0.735), feature concatenation (0.697; range, 0.673-0.721), and imaging-only (0.674; range, 0.666-0.680) models. High-risk patients had significantly shorter LRR-free survival than low-risk patients in all three folds (log-rank P < .001 for each). Smoking history and human papillomavirus status were the most influential clinical predictors. CONCLUSION: A multimodal cross-attention deep learning model integrating CT with clinical variables showed numerically better discrimination for LRR prediction in OPSCC than unimodal approaches. Prospective external validation is required before such models inform individualized treatment decisions.

Journal: Oral surgery, oral medicine, oral pathology and oral radiology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oooo.2026.09.010
Published: 2026-Sep-22

Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Odontogenic infections are common in oral and maxillofacial surgery. In some patients, further surgical drainage is needed. This study evaluated risk factors for reoperation in hospitalised patients with odontogenic infections. STUDY DESIGN: A retrospective, single-centre cohort study was conducted in 1,173 hospitalised patients treated for odontogenic infections between January 2014 and April 2020. Patients were divided into a reoperation group (n = 38) and a no-reoperation group (n = 1,135). RESULTS: Chronic renal failure (OR: 5.985, 95% CI: 2.174-16.475; P < .001), chronic respiratory disease (OR: 2.51, 95% CI: 1.031-6.261; P = .043), parapharyngeal space involvement (OR: 4.09, 95% CI: 1.873-8.943; P < .001), and buccal space 1 involvement (OR: 3.431, 95% CI: 1.283-9.179; P = .014) were associated with reoperation in univariable analysis. In multivariable analysis, parapharyngeal space involvement remained the strongest independent predictor (OR: 4.192, 95% CI: 1.676-10.487; P = .002). Admission C-reactive protein (CRP) was associated with reoperation in the available laboratory subset (OR: 1.064, 95% CI: 1.034-1.096; P < .001), but this should be interpreted cautiously because values were not available for all reoperated patients. CONCLUSIONS: Parapharyngeal space infection was the main predictor of reoperation. Chronic renal failure and chronic respiratory disease may increase risk. Admission C-reactive protein was associated with reoperation, but the small dataset limits interpretation.

item.title: Prognostic significance of systemic inflammatory and peripheral immune profiles in differentiated thyroid carcinoma: a retrospective cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Zhang X, Liu F, Wang W, Peng C, Qin Y
item.description:
Authors: Zhang X, Liu F, Wang W, Peng C, Qin Y
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16883-6
Published: 2026-Sep-04
PMID: 42995540



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although differentiated thyroid carcinoma (DTC) generally has a favorable prognosis, a subset of patients develop aggressive disease associated with poor outcomes. Current risk stratification relies mainly on clinicopathological features, whereas circulating inflammatory and immune biomarkers may provide complementary prognostic information. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic significance of systemic inflammatory status, thyroid-related biomarkers, and peripheral immune profiles in patients with DTC. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 430 patients with pathologically confirmed DTC who underwent surgical resection. Preoperative inflammatory markers, thyroid-related biomarkers, and peripheral immune cell profiles were evaluated, and their associations with overall survival (OS) were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression models. RESULTS: Compared with healthy controls and patients with benign thyroid nodules, patients with DTC exhibited significantly elevated levels of the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), thyroglobulin (Tg), and thyroglobulin antibody (TgAb) (all P < 0.001). Higher levels of SII, Tg, and TgAb were associated with lymph node metastasis and distant metastasis. Multivariable Cox regression analysis identified older age, follicular thyroid carcinoma, lymph node metastasis, distant metastasis, elevated SII, increased Tg and TgAb levels, and higher CD8⁺ T-cell proportion as independent predictors of inferior OS. Kaplan-Meier analyses further demonstrated that higher proportions of CD3+, CD4+, and CD19 + cells and lower proportions of CD56 + cells were associated with improved OS, whereas CD127 + cell proportion showed no significant association with OS. CONCLUSIONS: Systemic inflammatory status, thyroid-related biomarkers, and peripheral immune cell profiles provide complementary prognostic information in patients with DTC. Integration of SII, Tg/TgAb levels, and immune profiling may complement existing risk stratification approaches and facilitate individualized postoperative risk assessment and surveillance.

item.title: Role of CDC25B in human cancers: a meta-analysis and bioinformatics analysis.

Published: 2026-Aug-15

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: CDC25B, as an important member of the CDC25 family, plays a vital role in cell regulation. Recent studies have identified it as a potential oncogene implicated in tumorigenesis and cancer progression. The goal of our research was to shed light on the usefulness and significance of CDC25B as a reliable marker for predicting cancer outcomes. METHODS: The databases PubMed, Web of Science, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) and Wanfang data were used to find relevant articles published prior to May 30, 2025. The correlation between CDC25B expression and tumor prognosis or clinical features by calculating the overall hazard ratio or odds ratio and 95% confidence interval. To further verify our results, we also employed an online database from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and GTEx. RESULTS: Our study selected 16 articles for meta-analysis, including 2056 cancer patients. The current study showed that higher CDC25B expression was linked to poorer overall survival (OS) (HR =1.90, 95% CI: 1.45-2.48) and disease free survival (DFS) (HR =5.99, 95% CI: 1.07-33.63) in some cancers. The frequency of CDC25B gene alteration was highest in OV. GSEA analysis demonstrated that CDC25B was invoved in apoptosis and cell cycle in most tumors. CDC25B was correlated with immnue cell infiltration in cancers. CONCLUSION: Abnormal CDC25B expression is linked to the clinical prognosis and pathological characteristics of different cancers. CDC25B expression levels are only associated with prognosis in specific cancer types (KIRC, LIHC, UVM).

item.title: A cfDNA fragmentomics-based liquid biopsy assay for early detection of oral cancer.
item.dc:creator: Wang W, Ding T, Liu C, Hong X, He P, Yang W, Zhong M, Jiang Y
item.description:
Authors: Wang W, Ding T, Liu C, Hong X, He P, Yang W, Zhong M, Jiang Y
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16606-x
Published: 2026-Aug-15
PMID: 43009804



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early detection of oral cancer improves outcomes, but remains limited by the invasiveness and low sensitivity of current screening methods. METHODS: This study included 342 participants (200 in the training and 142 in the validation cohorts). Plasma cfDNA underwent low-depth whole-genome sequencing, with data normalized to a standardized 5× coverage via down-sampling to ensure consistent analysis. Three cfDNA-derived features, including fragment size ratio (FSR), copy number variation (CNV), and repetitive element profiles (REP), were extracted and integrated using a stacked machine learning ensemble to generate prediction scores. Model performance was evaluated by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity with 95% confidence intervals. RESULTS: In the training cohort, oral cancer patients had a median age of 53 years (91% male), while healthy individuals had a median age of 57 years (37% male). In the validation cohort, the median ages were 53 and 57 years, with male proportions of 83.1% and 38.0% in the cancer and healthy groups, respectively. Cancer samples exhibited shorter cfDNA fragments, recurrent CNV gains at 3q and 8q, and losses at 3p and 5q. The individual AUCs for FSR, CNV, and REP were 0.973, 0.983, and 0.979 in the training cohort, and 0.960, 0.982, and 0.972 in the validation cohort, respectively. The integrated stacked model achieved AUCs of 0.996 (95% CI: 0.991-1.000) and 0.988 (95% CI: 0.975-0.988) in the training and validation cohorts, respectively. To prioritize high specificity for large-scale screening, a decision threshold was established in the training cohort to target 98.0% specificity, which yielded a corresponding sensitivity of 98.0%. When this pre-fixed threshold was blindly applied to the independent validation cohort, a sensitivity of 94.4% and a specificity of 95.8% were achieved. Prediction scores were not significantly associated with age, sex, or tumor site. CONCLUSIONS: The cfDNA fragmentomics-based stacked model distinguished oral cancer from healthy individuals, including early stage disease, supporting its potential for noninvasive approach for oral cancer detection.

item.title: Microbial dysbiosis and treatment-related gastrointestinal adverse events in locoregionally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma: an exploratory study of the oral and gut microbiome.
item.dc:creator: Chen Y, Huang C, Qin Y, Jian Y, Li L, Li J, Meng Z, Kang M
item.description:
Authors: Chen Y, Huang C, Qin Y, Jian Y, Li L, Li J, Meng Z, Kang M
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16631-w
Published: 2026-Aug-14

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gastrointestinal adverse events are frequent during treatment for locoregionally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma (LA-NPC) and can impair nutritional status and treatment tolerance. Radiotherapy and chemotherapy may disrupt microbial communities, but whether oral and gut microbiota are associated with treatment-related gastrointestinal adverse events remains unclear. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Oral swab and stool samples from 80 patients with LA-NPC were analyzed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Associations between treatment-related gastrointestinal adverse events and oral microbial composition were evaluated, together with analyses of microbial functions and gut microbial profiles. Oral microbiota features were then used to develop machine learning models for distinguishing patients with gastrointestinal adverse events. RESULTS: Among 80 patients with LA-NPC, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and constipation occurred in 72.5%, 51.3%, 46.3%, and 67.5%, respectively. Oral microbiota analysis showed enrichment of Alloprevotella, Fusobacterium, and Campylobacter in patients with gastrointestinal adverse events or a high symptom burden, whereas Rothia and Streptococcus were enriched in those without events or with a low burden. Predicted oral microbial functions involved propanoate metabolism, lipoic acid metabolism, retinol metabolism, glycan degradation, sphingolipid metabolism, calcium signaling, and lipopolysaccharide biosynthesis. Alterations in specific gut genera, including Helicobacter, Parasutterella, and Anaerotruncus, were also observed. CONCLUSIONS: This study identified oral and gut microbial features associated with treatment-related gastrointestinal adverse events in patients with LA-NPC. Oral microbial features showed potential value for classifying gastrointestinal adverse event status during treatment.

item.title: Pre-treatment serum bicarbonate predicts survival in patients with locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma undergoing definitive radiotherapy: a retrospective propensity score matching study.
item.dc:creator: Ji H, Zhang P, Wang Y, Su Y, Si H, Jia Y, Qiao X, Zhou Z
item.description:
Authors: Ji H, Zhang P, Wang Y, Su Y, Si H, Jia Y, Qiao X, Zhou Z
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16723-7
Published: 2026-Aug-14
PMID: 43009855



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of pre-treatment serum bicarbonate (HCO3-) for overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) in locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (LA-ESCC) patients undergoing definitive radiotherapy. METHODS: Patients with stage Ⅱ-Ⅳa ESCC treated with definitive radiotherapy between 2015 and 2022 were screened and then divided into Group A (high HCO3-) and Group B (low HCO3-). Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed using sex, age, ECOG score, body mass index, tumor length, tumor location, clinical T category, clinical N category, clinical TNM stage, combined chemotherapy, and radiation dose as covariates at a 1:2 ratio (Group A: Group B). OS and PFS were compared between different groups using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression analysis. RESULTS: A total of 301 patients were included in the study. The median follow-up time was 54.1 months. The median OS and PFS were 17.3 months and 11.0 months. The median HCO3- was 24.9 mmol/L. Before PSM, the median OS was 27.0 months in Group A (HCO3- ≥26 mmol/L, n = 103) and 14.8 months in Group B (HCO3- <26 mmol/L, n = 198), p < 0.0001. The median PFS was 16.3 months in Group A and 9.6 months in Group B, p = 0.0002. After 1:2 PSM, the median OS was 25.7 months in Group A (n = 97) and 15.3 months in Group B (n = 169), p = 0.0011. The median PFS was 13.0 months in Group A and 9.6 months in Group B, p = 0.0059. Multivariate Cox analysis suggested that age ≥ 66 (HR 0.739, p = 0.036), T category < 3 (HR 0.484, p < 0.001), clinical N category < 2 (HR 0.713, p = 0.022), combined chemotherapy (HR 0.625, p = 0.003), and HCO3- ≥26 mmol/L (HR 0.656, p = 0.004) were independent favorable prognostic factors for OS. Clinical T category < 3 (HR 0.565, p < 0.001), clinical stage Ⅱ-Ⅲ (HR 0.685, p = 0.019), and pre-treatment HCO3- ≥26 mmol/L (HR 0.717, p = 0.019) were independent favorable prognostic factors for PFS. CONCLUSIONS: A high pre-treatment serum bicarbonate level is associated with an increased OS and PFS in LA-ESCC patients undergoing definitive radiotherapy. Therefore, pre-treatment serum bicarbonate may serve as a readily available prognostic biomarker to inform risk stratification and treatment planning in LA-ESCC patients undergoing definitive radiotherapy.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dual-layer multileaf collimator (MLC) accelerators, such as Halcyon, are increasingly used in clinical settings; however, the ability of treatment planning systems (TPS) to effectively optimize treatment plans for such accelerators remains an important consideration. PURPOSE: This study evaluates the feasibility of using uTPS to optimize treatment plans for dual-layer MLC accelerators, with Eclipse as a clinical reference. METHODS: Standard radiation data from the Halcyon 2.0 accelerator were used to model the beam in the uTPS (Shanghai United Imaging Healthcare Co., Ltd., version R001). Twenty cases were selected, with five each for hypopharyngeal, esophageal, breast, and cervical cancers. Volumetric modulated arc therapy plans were generated using the uTPS stochastic platform optimizer and the Eclipse photon optimizer (PO). All plans were calculated using the Acuros external beam (AXB) algorithm for dosimetric comparison. Key indicators, such as the conformity index (CI), homogeneity index (HI), and organ-at-risk (OAR) doses, were analyzed and compared. The feasibility of delivering uTPS plans on the Halcyon accelerator was validated. The dosimetric accuracy was confirmed using ArcCheck, and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction were performed. RESULTS: uTPS and Eclipse plans exhibited similar dosimetric qualities for esophageal and cervical cancer cases, with no significant differences in CI, HI, and OAR doses. However, uTPS demonstrated superior OAR sparing in specific cases: in hypopharyngeal cancer, uTPS significantly reduced the brainstem [Formula: see text] by 34.48%, the left parotid[Formula: see text] by 11.8%, and the left parotid [Formula: see text] by 6.9% (all P < 0.05); in breast cancer, uTPS significantly reduced the spinal cord [Formula: see text]by 49.6% (P < 0.05). No statistically significant differences were observed in other dosimetric parameters. No significant differences in total monitor units were observed between the uTPS and Eclipse plans. All uTPS plans were successfully delivered on the Halcyon accelerator, with gamma passing rates exceeding 97%. CONCLUSIONS: The commercially available uTPS supports effective plan optimization for dual-layer MLC Halcyon accelerators, offering plan quality comparable to that of Eclipse.

item.title: Prognostic evaluation of stage I-IVa nasopharyngeal carcinoma: integrating PET/CT parameters, inflammatory and clinical features.

Authors: Lv Y, Zheng D, Zhou Z, Dai Z, Wei S, Lan X, Gao Z, Qin C
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16679-8
Published: 2026-Aug-12
PMID: 43015633



Abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate prognostic 18F-FDG PET/CT parameters and develop a nomogram integrating inflammatory markers and clinicopathological characteristics for predicting progression-free survival (PFS) in stage I-IVa nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). METHODS: Stage I-IVa NPC patients who underwent pretreatment 18F-FDG PET/CT were retrospectively collected. The 18F-FDG PET and clinicopathologic parameters were analyzed. The correlation among PET parameters was evaluated with Spearman's rho test. ROC curve was used to evaluate the predictive performance and calculate the optimal cut-off values for grouping. The survival analyses were performed by Kaplan-Meier analysis and log-rank test. Prognostic factors were identified using Cox regression, and a nomogram was constructed and validated. RESULTS: Eighty‑six patients were enrolled (63 [73.26%] males, mean age 48.38 ± 11.91 years). Heterogeneity factor (HF) and metabolic tumor volume (MTV) showed strong correlation (r = 0.88, P < 0.01). ROC curve analysis indicated HF and MTV exhibited good predictive value for 1-, 3-, and 5-year PFS (HF: AUC = 0.817, 0.678, and 0.672; MTV: AUC = 0.866, 0.685, and 0.670), with the best prognostic efficacy for 1-year PFS. HF, systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), overall stage, and concurrent chemoradiotherapy were independent predictors of 5-year PFS. The nomogram demonstrated high predictive ability for PFS, with AUCs of 0.83-0.86 and a C-index of 0.78, further supported by its clinical utility. CONCLUSION: The novel multifactor nomogram combining HF with SII, overall stage, and treatment strategy (concurrent chemoradiotherapy) demonstrates superior prognostic predictive performance, improving accuracy and enabling personalized assessment in I-IVa stage NPC patients management.
